The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, for items not specified in the national pollutant discharge standards, formulate local pollutant discharge standards; for items already specified in the national pollutant discharge standards, they may formulate local pollutant discharge standards that are stricter than the national pollutant discharge standards. Local pollutant discharge standards shall be reported to the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council for recordation.

Article 154 The formulation of pollutant discharge standards shall be based on ecological environmental quality standards and economic and technical conditions, reflect the characteristics of pollutant discharge and acceptable ecological environmental risks, and scientifically and reasonably determine the control requirements for pollutant discharge.

Article 155 The state shall implement a total discharge control system for key pollutants.
The total discharge control indicators for key pollutants shall, by the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council, after soliciting opinions from relevant departments and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, be submitted to the State Council for approval and issued for implementation jointly with the development and reform department of the State Council. The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall decompose and implement the total control indicators issued by the State Council, and control or reduce the total discharge of key pollutants within their respective administrative regions.
The specific measures for determining and decomposing the total control indicators shall be formulated by the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council jointly with relevant departments.

Article 156 The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, based on the ecological environmental quality status of their respective administrative regions and the needs of pollution prevention and control work, implement total discharge control for other key pollutants beyond those determined by the state.
Article 157 Enterprises and institutions shall comply with the total discharge control indicators for key pollutants that have been decomposed and assigned to the unit.

Article 158 For areas that exceed the total discharge control indicators for key pollutants or fail to achieve the ecological environmental quality objectives, the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall suspend the approval of the ecological environmental impact report and the ecological environmental impact statement form for construction projects that would increase the total discharge of key pollutants in that area.

Article 159 The competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall, jointly with relevant departments, conduct interviews with the principal leaders of local people's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments in areas with prominent environmental pollution problems, ineffective prevention and control work, and strong public complaints, and require them to take effective measures to rectify in a timely manner. The status of rectification after the interview shall be disclosed to the public.

Article 160 The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall, according to law, organize the implementation of statistical surveys of emission sources, and establish and improve the statistical accounting method system and data quality control system for emission sources. The state shall regularly organize the implementation of a national pollution source survey.
Article 161 The department of ecology and environment of the State Council shall, together with relevant departments, establish and improve a pollution damage assessment system.

Article 162 The pollution prevention and control facilities in a construction project shall be designed, constructed, and put into operation simultaneously with the main project. The pollution prevention and control facilities shall comply with the requirements of the approved environmental impact report and environmental impact statement, and shall not be dismantled or left idle without authorization.
Before a construction project is put into production or use, the construction unit shall, according to national regulations, carry out acceptance inspection of the supporting pollution prevention and control facilities.

Article 163 Enterprises, public institutions, and other business operators that discharge pollutants shall, in accordance with laws and regulations and the provisions of the department of ecology and environment of the State Council, set up and use pollutant discharge outlets (hereinafter referred to as discharge outlets).

Article 164 It is prohibited to discharge pollutants by means of evading supervision, such as through hidden pipes, seepage wells, seepage pits, injection, fissures, karst caves, tampering with or falsifying monitoring data, temporary production suspension for the purpose of evading on-site inspection, opening emergency discharge channels in non-emergency situations, abnormal operation of pollution prevention and control facilities, etc.
It is prohibited to dump, pile up, or store solid waste and other pollutants into rivers, lakes, canals, channels, reservoirs, and the beaches and banks below their highest water level lines, as well as other locations specified by laws and regulations.

Article 165 People's governments at all levels shall make overall plans and construct urban and rural sewage treatment facilities and supporting pipe networks, solid waste collection, transportation, and disposal facilities and sites, as well as other pollution prevention and control facilities, and shall ensure their normal operation, so as to improve the construction level of urban and rural pollution prevention and control facilities.
Article 166 The department of ecology and environment of the State Council shall regularly publish a guiding catalogue of pollution prevention and control technologies, processes, and equipment.

Article 167 The State shall gradually promote emission rights trading for key air pollutants, water pollutants, etc., establish and improve an emission rights trading system for total emission control indicators of key pollutants, and strengthen supervision and management over the entire process of emission rights trading.
Article 168 Enterprises, public institutions, and other business operators that directly discharge taxable pollutants into the environment shall pay environmental protection tax according to law.
Article 169 The State encourages the purchase of environmental pollution liability insurance.

Article 170 People's governments at all levels shall allocate funds in their fiscal budgets to support work such as the protection of rural drinking water sources, treatment of domestic sewage, disposal of domestic garbage and other waste, prevention and control of agricultural non-point source pollution, prevention and control of pollution from livestock and poultry breeding and slaughtering, prevention and control of aquaculture pollution, prevention and control of soil pollution, and treatment of pollution from rural industrial and mining enterprises.

Article 171 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments and institutions such as agriculture and rural affairs shall guide agricultural producers and operators in scientific planting and breeding, scientifically, rationally, and safely use pesticides, veterinary drugs, feed and feed additives, fertilizers and other agricultural inputs, scientifically dispose of agricultural films, crop straw, packaging waste of agricultural inputs and other agricultural wastes, strengthen control over pollutants discharged in agricultural production and operation activities, and prevent agricultural non-point source pollution.
It is prohibited to apply to farmland solid waste and wastewater that do not meet agricultural standards and ecological and environmental protection standards. When applying pesticides, fertilizers and other agricultural inputs and when irrigating, effective measures shall be taken to prevent heavy metals and other toxic and hazardous substances from polluting the environment.
The site selection, construction, and management of livestock and poultry farms, designated slaughtering enterprises, etc. shall comply with the provisions of laws and regulations. Livestock and poultry farms shall improve the level of precision feeding and strengthen comprehensive management of livestock and poultry manure and sewage. Units and individuals engaged in livestock and poultry breeding and slaughtering shall take effective measures to timely collect, store, transport, treat harmlessly, and utilize as resources livestock and poultry manure, carcasses and other waste, and prevent environmental pollution.
People's governments at the county level shall be responsible for organizing the disposal of rural domestic waste.

Article 172 The State shall strengthen systematic treatment in regions with prominent agricultural non-point source pollution, and improve the effectiveness of agricultural non-point source pollution prevention and control.

Article 173 The department of ecology and environment of the State Council shall, together with relevant departments, determine key areas and key industries for heavy metal pollution prevention and control, and submit them to the State Council for approval. The local people's governments at or above the level of a city divided into districts where the key areas are located shall, according to national regulations, organize the formulation and implementation of heavy metal pollution prevention and control plans. Enterprises in key industries shall regularly conduct hazard investigation and remediation, and take effective measures to prevent and control heavy metal pollution.

Article 174 The State shall establish and improve a supervision and management system for stationary pollution sources with the emission permit system as the core, and the specific measures shall be formulated by the State Council.
Enterprises, public institutions, and other business operators subject to emission permit management shall obtain an emission permit according to regulations; those that have not obtained an emission permit shall not discharge pollutants.

Article 175 Based on factors such as the amount of pollutants generated, the amount discharged, and the degree of impact on the ecological environment, enterprises, public institutions, and other business operators subject to emission permit management shall be subject to classified management of emission permits:
(1) Where the amount of pollutants generated, the amount discharged, or the degree of impact on the ecological environment is relatively large, key management of emission permits shall be implemented;
(2) Where the amount of pollutants generated, the amount discharged, and the degree of impact on the ecological environment are all relatively small, simplified management of emission permits shall be implemented.
The scope, implementation steps, and list of management categories of enterprises, public institutions, and other business operators subject to emission permit management shall be drafted by the department of ecology and environment of the State Council and, after being submitted to the State Council for approval, shall be published and implemented. When formulating the scope, implementation steps, and list of management categories of enterprises, public institutions, and other business operators subject to emission permit management, opinions from relevant departments, industry associations, enterprises, public institutions, and the public shall be solicited.

Article 177 The department of ecology and environment of the local people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts shall strengthen the supervision and management of emission permits.

Article 178 Enterprises, public institutions, and other business operators shall apply to the department of ecology and environment of the local people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts where their production and business operation premises are located for obtaining an emission permit.
If a marine engineering project needs to obtain an emission permit, it shall apply to the department of ecology and environment of the State Council or its sea area agency dispatched by the department.

Article 179 An emission permit is the main basis for ecological and environmental supervision and management of enterprises, public institutions, and other business operators subject to emission permit management.
Enterprises, public institutions, and other business operators subject to emission permit management shall comply with the requirements of the emission permit, operate and maintain pollution prevention and control facilities according to regulations, establish an ecological and environmental management system, and strictly control pollutant discharge.

Article 183 Any enterprise, public institution, or other producer or business operator that is subject to pollutant discharge permit management shall, in accordance with the requirements of the pollutant discharge permit and relevant standards and norms, conduct self-monitoring according to law, establish management records, and keep the original monitoring records and management records. The retention period for original monitoring records and management records shall not be less than five years.

Article 184 Any enterprise, public institution, or other producer or business operator that is subject to key pollutant discharge permit management shall, in accordance with state provisions, install, use, and maintain automatic monitoring equipment for pollutant discharge, carry out monitoring and automatic monitoring, and connect with the monitoring equipment of the competent department of ecological environment, ensure the normal operation of automatic monitoring equipment, and keep original monitoring records. The specific measures for monitoring shall be formulated by the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council.
Where an enterprise, public institution, or other producer or business operator subject to key pollutant discharge permit management discovers that the data transmitted by the automatic monitoring equipment for pollutant discharge is abnormal, it shall promptly report to the competent department of ecological environment and carry out inspection and repair. Where the competent department of ecological environment discovers that the data transmitted by the automatic monitoring equipment for pollutant discharge of an enterprise, public institution, or other producer or business operator subject to key pollutant discharge permit management is abnormal, it shall promptly conduct an investigation.

Article 185 Any enterprise, public institution, or other producer or business operator that is subject to pollutant discharge permit management shall, in accordance with the provisions, disclose to the public the types, concentration and amount of pollutants discharged, as well as the construction and operation of pollution prevention and control facilities, self-monitoring data and other pollutant discharge information, and shall accept public supervision.

Article 186 Any enterprise, public institution, or other producer or business operator with very small amounts of pollutant generation and discharge and a very small degree of impact on the ecological environment shall fill in a pollutant discharge registration form and shall not be subject to pollutant discharge permit management. The pollutant discharge registration form shall be valid for five years.
The list of the scope of enterprises, public institutions, and other producers or business operators that are required to fill in the pollutant discharge registration form shall be formulated and published by the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council. The formulation of the list of the scope of enterprises, public institutions, and other producers or business operators that are required to fill in the pollutant discharge registration form shall seek the opinions of relevant departments, industry associations, enterprises, public institutions, and the public, among others.
Division 2 Prevention and Control of Atmospheric Pollution
Article 187 This Division applies to the prevention and control of atmospheric pollution.

Article 188 For the purposes of this Law, “atmospheric pollution” means the phenomenon where the atmosphere, due to the introduction of a certain substance, undergoes changes in its chemical, physical or other characteristics, endangering public health or damaging the ecological environment, thereby causing deterioration of the atmospheric environmental quality.

Article 189 The prevention and control of atmospheric pollution shall aim at improving the quality of the atmospheric environment, transforming the mode of economic development, optimizing the industrial structure and layout, and adjusting the energy structure and the transportation structure.
The prevention and control of atmospheric pollution shall strengthen the comprehensive prevention and control of atmospheric pollution from coal combustion, industry, motor vehicles and vessels, non-road mobile machinery, fugitive dust, agriculture, etc., promote regional joint prevention and control of atmospheric pollution, and implement coordinated control of atmospheric pollutants and greenhouse gases, including particulate matter, sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, volatile organic compounds, ammonia, etc.

Article 190 The local people's government at or above the city with districts level shall formulate plans and take effective measures to control or gradually reduce the discharge of atmospheric pollutants, so that the atmospheric environment quality meets the prescribed standards and is progressively improved.

Article 191 The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall carry out unified supervision and administration of the prevention and control of atmospheric pollution nationwide. The competent department of ecological environment of a local people's government shall carry out unified supervision and administration of the prevention and control of atmospheric pollution within its administrative region.
Other relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level shall carry out supervision and administration of the prevention and control of atmospheric pollution within the scope of their respective duties.

Article 192 The people's government of a municipality directly under the Central Government, a city with districts, or a county in an area that has not met the national atmospheric environmental quality standards shall promptly formulate a plan for meeting the atmospheric environmental quality standards within a time limit, take effective measures, and meet the atmospheric environmental quality standards within the time limit prescribed by the people's government at or above the provincial level.

Article 193 The plan for meeting the atmospheric environmental quality standards within a time limit formulated by the people's government of a municipality directly under the Central Government or a city with districts shall be reported to the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council for record.

Article 194 The plan for meeting the atmospheric environmental quality standards within a time limit shall be evaluated and revised in a timely manner based on the requirements of atmospheric pollution prevention and control and the economic and technical conditions.

Article 195 Quality standards for coal, petroleum coke, biomass fuel, products containing volatile organic compounds such as coatings, fireworks and firecrackers, and products such as boilers shall specify the requirements for the prevention and control of atmospheric pollution.
Quality standards for fuel oil shall comply with the national requirements for controlling atmospheric pollutants and shall be coordinated with the national emission standards for atmospheric pollutants from motor vehicles and vessels and non-road mobile machinery, and shall be implemented simultaneously.

Article 196 The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall organize the monitoring of atmospheric environmental quality and atmospheric pollution sources, and organize the construction and management of a national monitoring network for atmospheric environmental quality and atmospheric pollution sources.
The competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government at or above the city with districts level shall be responsible for organizing the construction and management of the monitoring network for atmospheric environmental quality and atmospheric pollution sources within its administrative region, and carry out monitoring of atmospheric environmental quality and atmospheric pollution sources.

Article 197 Any enterprise, public institution, or other producer or business operator shall, in accordance with state provisions, monitor the industrial waste gases and toxic and hazardous atmospheric pollutants it discharges, and keep original monitoring records. The specific measures for monitoring shall be formulated by the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council.

Article 198 The competent department of ecological environment shall promptly monitor the atmospheric pollutants generated by sudden environmental pollution incidents and disclose the monitoring information to the public.

Article 199 The State encourages and supports the analysis of the sources of atmospheric pollution and their changing trends, and gives play to the supporting role of science and technology in the prevention and control of atmospheric pollution.
Article 200 The prevention and control of atmospheric pollution from marine engineering projects shall not be subject to this Division.

Article 201 The relevant departments of the State Council and local people's governments at all levels shall optimize the manner of coal usage and reduce the discharge of atmospheric pollutants during the processes of coal production, storage, transportation, usage, and conversion.

Article 202 The State promotes coal washing and processing to reduce the sulfur and ash content of coal and restricts the mining of coal with high sulfur and ash content. Newly built coal mines shall simultaneously construct supporting coal washing facilities so that the sulfur and ash content of the coal meets the prescribed standards; for existing coal mines, except where the coal mined has low sulfur and low ash content or where washing is not required based on the requirements of coal-fired power plants that have achieved emission standards, supporting coal washing facilities shall be constructed within a prescribed time limit.
It is prohibited to mine coal whose content of toxic and hazardous substances such as radioactivity and arsenic exceeds the prescribed standards.
Article 203 Entities engaged in the extraction and utilization of coalbed methane shall ensure that the discharge of coalbed methane complies with the relevant standards and specifications.

Article 204 It is prohibited to import, sell, or burn coal that does not meet quality standards, and the use of high-quality coal is encouraged.
Entities storing materials such as coal, coal gangue, coal slag, and coal ash shall take measures to prevent spontaneous combustion and to prevent air pollution.

Article 205 Local people's governments at all levels shall take effective measures to strengthen the management of bulk coal, prohibit the sale of coal that does not meet the quality standards for bulk coal, and encourage and support the adoption of measures such as clean low-carbon energy and centralized heating to replace the burning of bulk coal and prevent air pollution caused thereby.

Article 206 Petroleum refining enterprises shall produce fuel oil in accordance with fuel oil quality standards.
It is prohibited to import, sell, or use petroleum coke that does not meet quality standards.

Article 207 Local people's governments at or above the level of a city divided into districts may designate and publish areas where the burning of high-pollution fuels is prohibited, and shall gradually expand the scope of such areas based on the requirements for improving the quality of the atmospheric environment. The catalogue of high-pollution fuels shall be determined by the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council.
Within the prohibited burning areas, it is prohibited to sell or burn high-pollution fuels; it is prohibited to construct or expand facilities that burn high-pollution fuels, and existing facilities shall, within a time limit prescribed by the local people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts, switch to natural gas, shale gas, liquefied petroleum gas, electricity, or other clean low-carbon energy.

Article 208 Urban construction shall be planned in a coordinated manner, and in coal-fired heating areas, combined heat and power generation and centralized heating shall be promoted. In areas covered by a centralized heating pipeline network, it is prohibited to construct or expand dispersed coal-fired heating boilers; existing coal-fired heating boilers that cannot meet emission standards shall be dismantled within a time limit prescribed by the local people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts.

Article 209 The administrative departments for market regulation of people's governments at or above the county level shall, in conjunction with the competent departments of ecological environment, supervise and inspect the implementation of air pollution prevention and control standards or requirements in the production, import, sale, and use of boilers; boilers that do not meet the air pollution prevention and control standards or requirements shall not be produced, imported, sold, or used.

Article 210 Coal-fired power plants and other coal-burning entities shall adopt clean production processes, construct supporting facilities for dust removal, desulfurization, denitrification, etc., or take other measures such as technological transformation to control the discharge of atmospheric pollutants.
The State encourages coal-burning entities to adopt advanced technologies and facilities for the synergistic control of atmospheric pollutants such as dust removal, desulfurization, denitrification, and mercury removal to reduce the discharge of atmospheric pollutants.

Article 211 Enterprises in industries such as iron and steel, building materials, non-ferrous metals, petroleum, and chemicals that discharge dust, sulfides, and nitrogen oxides during production shall adopt clean production processes, construct supporting facilities for dust removal, desulfurization, denitrification, etc., or take other measures such as technological transformation to control the discharge of atmospheric pollutants.

Article 212 The State encourages and supports key industries such as iron and steel, cement, and coking, as well as coal-fired boilers, to adopt technologies such as ultra-low emissions to reduce the discharge of atmospheric pollutants.

Article 213 The relevant departments of the State Council shall, within their respective functions and duties, formulate standards for the limit values of volatile organic compound (VOC) content in raw and auxiliary materials and products containing VOCs, and standards for raw and auxiliary materials and products with low VOC content.
Entities that produce, import, sell, or use raw and auxiliary materials and products containing VOCs shall ensure that the VOC content meets the quality standards or requirements.
The State encourages the production, import, sale, and use of raw and auxiliary materials and products with low toxicity and low VOC content, and industrial coating enterprises and others shall use raw and auxiliary materials and products with low VOC content in accordance with the provisions.

Article 214 The production and use of raw and auxiliary materials and products containing VOCs shall be carried out in enclosed spaces or equipment and with pollution prevention and control facilities installed and used, or other effective measures shall be taken to reduce exhaust emissions, in accordance with State provisions.
Article 215 The State shall establish and improve a labeling system for low VOC content in products, and producers of products with low VOC content shall label them in accordance with the provisions.

Article 216 Enterprises in the petroleum, chemical, and other industries that produce or use organic solvents shall take effective measures to conduct daily maintenance and repair of pipelines and equipment to reduce material leaks, and shall promptly collect and treat leaked materials.
Oil storage depots, gas stations, crude oil and refined oil terminals, crude oil and refined oil transport vessels, tanker trucks, and railway tank cars, among others, shall install vapor recovery devices in accordance with State provisions and maintain their normal use.

Article 217 Enterprises in industries such as iron and steel, building materials, non-ferrous metals, petroleum, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and mining, as well as other industrial production enterprises, shall strengthen refined management and adopt measures such as centralized collection and treatment to strictly control the discharge of dust and gaseous pollutants.
Industrial production enterprises shall take measures such as enclosure, shielding, covering, cleaning, and sprinkling to reduce the emission of dust and gaseous pollutants generated during the storage, transfer, loading, and unloading of materials within their premises.

Article 218 Combustible gases generated from industrial production, landfill, and other activities shall be recovered and utilized. Where recovery and utilization conditions are not available, pollution prevention and control treatment shall be carried out.
If the recovery and utilization device for combustible gases cannot operate normally, it shall be repaired or updated promptly. If it is necessary to discharge combustible gases during the period when the recovery and utilization device is not operating normally, the discharged combustible gases shall be fully combusted or other measures to control the discharge of atmospheric pollutants shall be taken, and the local competent department of ecological environment shall be notified, and the device shall be repaired or updated within the prescribed time limit as required.

Article 219 The State advocates green travel, reasonably controls the number of fuel-powered motor vehicles based on urban planning, vigorously develops urban public transport, and increases the proportion of trips made by public transport.
The State adopts measures such as fiscal, tax, and government procurement to promote and apply energy-saving, environmentally friendly, and new energy motor vehicles, vessels, and non-road mobile machinery, limits the development of motor vehicles, vessels, and non-road mobile machinery with high fuel consumption and high emissions, and reduces the consumption of fossil energy.
People's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, in areas where conditions permit, implement in advance the emission limits for the corresponding phase of the national motor vehicle air pollutant emission standards, and shall report this to the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council for recordation.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen and improve urban traffic management, optimize road layout, and ensure the continuity and smoothness of pedestrian walkways and non-motor vehicle lanes.

Article 220 Key vehicle-using entities that make heavy use of heavy-duty trucks shall, in accordance with State provisions, incorporate the management of emissions during transport and loading/unloading into their unit's pollution prevention and control responsibility system, and strengthen the prevention and control of air pollution from heavy-duty trucks.

Article 221 Motor vehicles, vessels, non-road mobile machinery and their engines shall not discharge atmospheric pollutants exceeding the standards.
The production, import or sale of motor vehicles, vessels, non-road mobile machinery and their engines that do not meet the atmospheric pollutant emission standards is prohibited.

Article 222 Manufacturers of motor vehicles, non-road mobile machinery and their engines shall conduct emission inspections on newly produced motor vehicles, non-road mobile machinery and their engines. Only those that pass the inspection may leave the factory for sale. The inspection information shall be disclosed to the public and reported to the competent department of ecology and environment for recordation.
The competent departments of ecology and environment of the people's governments at or above the provincial level may, through on-site inspections, sampling tests and other means, strengthen the supervision and inspection of the atmospheric pollutant emission status and the operation of emission control systems of newly produced, imported and sold motor vehicles, non-road mobile machinery and their engines. The relevant departments of industry and information technology, transportation, market supervision and administration, and customs shall provide cooperation.

Article 223 In-use motor vehicles shall be subject to periodic emission inspections by motor vehicle emission inspection agencies in accordance with the provisions. Only those that pass the inspection may drive on roads. For those that have not passed the inspection, the traffic management department of the public security organ shall not issue a safety technical inspection合格标志 (passing mark).
The competent department of ecology and environment may conduct supervisory sampling tests on the atmospheric pollutant emission status and the operation of emission control systems of in-use motor vehicles at centralized parking lots, repair sites and heavy-duty vehicle use sites; without affecting normal traffic, it may conduct supervisory sampling tests on the atmospheric pollutant emission status and the operation of emission control systems of motor vehicles running on roads through non-contact road monitoring and other technical means, and the traffic management department of the public security organ shall provide cooperation.
For the purposes of this Law, "emission control systems" refer to systems such as pollution control, emission diagnosis, and remote emission management terminals installed on motor vehicles, vessels, non-road mobile machinery, etc.

Article 224 The competent department of ecology and environment shall, together with the relevant departments of transportation, housing and urban-rural construction, agriculture and rural affairs, and water administration, conduct supervision and inspection on the atmospheric pollutant emission status and the operation of emission control systems of in-use non-road mobile machinery; those with unqualified emissions shall not be used.
The maritime administration agency and the competent department of fisheries and fishery administration shall, within their respective functions and duties, conduct supervision and inspection on the atmospheric pollutant emission status and the operation of emission control systems of vessels; those with unqualified emissions shall not be used.

Article 225 Motor vehicle and non-road mobile machinery emission inspection agencies shall pass metrological certification according to law, use motor vehicle and non-road mobile machinery emission inspection equipment that has been verified as qualified according to law, conduct emission inspections on motor vehicles and non-road mobile machinery in accordance with the standards formulated by the competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council, and connect to the network of the competent department of ecology and environment to achieve real-time sharing of inspection data. Motor vehicle and non-road mobile machinery emission inspection agencies and their responsible persons shall be responsible for the authenticity, accuracy and completeness of the inspection data.
The competent department of ecology and environment and the certification and accreditation supervision and administration department shall, within their respective functions and duties, conduct supervision and inspection on the emission inspection situations of motor vehicle and non-road mobile machinery emission inspection agencies.

Article 226 Enterprises that produce or import motor vehicles and non-road mobile machinery shall disclose to the public the emission inspection information, pollution control technical information and relevant maintenance technical information of the motor vehicle models and non-road mobile machinery models they produce or import.
Maintenance units of motor vehicles and non-road mobile machinery shall, in accordance with the requirements for prevention and control of atmospheric pollution and relevant national technical specifications, repair in-use motor vehicles and non-road mobile machinery so that they meet the emission standards. The relevant departments of transportation, ecology and environment, etc., shall strengthen supervision and management according to law within their respective functions and duties.
The owners of motor vehicles, vessels and non-road mobile machinery shall not pass the emission inspections of motor vehicles, vessels and non-road mobile machinery by fraudulent means such as temporary replacement, tampering, shielding or falsification of emission control systems. Maintenance units of motor vehicles, vessels and non-road mobile machinery shall not provide such maintenance services. It is prohibited to damage, remove, tamper with, shield or falsify the emission control systems of motor vehicles, vessels and non-road mobile machinery.

Article 227 The State shall establish and improve the environmental recall system for motor vehicles and non-road mobile machinery.
If a production or import enterprise becomes aware that a motor vehicle or non-road mobile machinery does not meet the atmospheric pollutant emission standards or has an unreasonable discharge of atmospheric pollutants, and such situation is due to design or production defects, the enterprise shall recall it; if it fails to recall, the market supervision and administration department of the State Council shall, together with the competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council, order it to recall.

Article 228 If in-use heavy-duty vehicles, vessels, non-road mobile machinery, etc., have not installed emission control systems according to the provisions, or their emission control systems do not meet the requirements and cannot meet the emission standards, they shall be retrofitted with or replaced by emission control systems that meet the requirements, or other effective measures shall be taken.

Article 229 If in-use motor vehicles, non-road mobile machinery, etc., discharge atmospheric pollutants exceeding the standards, they shall be repaired; if, after repair or after adopting pollution control technologies, the discharge of atmospheric pollutants still does not meet the national emission standards, they shall be compulsorily scrapped. Their owners shall sell such motor vehicles, non-road mobile machinery, etc., to scrapped vehicle recycling and dismantling enterprises, which shall carry out registration, dismantling, destruction and other treatments in accordance with the national provisions.
The State encourages and supports the early scrapping of high-emission motor vehicles, vessels, non-road mobile machinery, etc.

Article 230 Local people's governments at or above the county level may, based on the status of atmospheric environmental quality, delineate and publish areas where the use of high-emission non-road mobile machinery is prohibited.

Article 231 Vessel inspection agencies shall conduct emission inspections on vessel engines and related equipment. Only after passing the inspection and meeting the national emission standards may a vessel be operated.

Article 232 Non-road mobile machinery inspection agencies shall conduct emission inspections on in-use non-road mobile machinery. Only after passing the inspection and meeting the national emission standards may they be operated.

Article 233 It is prohibited to produce, import or sell devices used to tamper with, shield or falsify the emission inspection data of motor vehicles, vessels, non-road mobile machinery and their engines, and inspection equipment that provides conditions for false emission inspections.

Article 234 Inland river vessels and vessels navigating directly between rivers and seas shall use fuel that meets the standards. Ocean-going vessels, after berthing, shall use fuel that meets the requirements for atmospheric pollutant control.

Article 235 Newly built wharves shall plan, design and construct shore-side power supply facilities according to the provisions; existing wharves shall gradually implement the renovation of shore-side power supply facilities according to the provisions. Vessels that have conditions for using shore power shall, after berthing, use shore power in accordance with the national provisions, except those using clean and low-carbon energy. Port operators and shore power supply enterprises that have the ability to supply shore power shall provide shore power to vessels that have conditions for using shore power in accordance with the national provisions.

Article 236 It is prohibited to produce, import or sell fuels and nitrogen oxide reducing agents for motor vehicles, vessels, and non-road mobile machinery that do not meet the standards; it is prohibited to sell non-motor-vehicle/vessel fuels to motor vehicles, non-road mobile machinery, inland river vessels and vessels navigating directly between rivers and seas; it is prohibited for motor vehicles, non-road mobile machinery, inland river vessels and vessels navigating directly between rivers and seas to use non-motor-vehicle/vessel fuels.

Article 237 The content of toxic and harmful substances and other atmospheric pollution prevention and control indicators in engine oils, nitrogen oxide reducing agents, fuel and lubricant additives and other additives shall meet the requirements of relevant standards, shall not impair the effectiveness and durability of the emission control systems of motor vehicles, vessels and non-road mobile machinery, and shall not increase new atmospheric pollutant emissions.

Article 238 The State actively promotes the prevention and control of atmospheric pollution by civil aircraft, and encourages the adoption of effective measures during design, production and use to reduce atmospheric pollutant emissions.
Civil aircraft shall meet the relevant engine emission requirements in the airworthiness standards prescribed by the competent civil aviation authority of the State Council.
The atmospheric pollutant emissions of in-use railway diesel locomotives shall meet the national emission standards.

Article 239 Local people's governments at all levels shall strengthen the management of construction and transportation, keep roads clean, control the stacking of material piles and muck, expand the area of green spaces, water bodies, wetlands and ground paving, and prevent and control dust pollution.
The relevant departments of housing and urban-rural construction, city appearance and environmental sanitation, transportation, and natural resources shall, according to the functions and duties determined by the people's government at the corresponding level, properly carry out the work of dust pollution prevention and control.

Article 240 The construction unit shall include the costs of dust pollution prevention and control in the project cost, and specify in the construction contract the responsibility of the construction entity for dust pollution prevention and control. The construction entity shall formulate specific implementation plans for construction dust pollution prevention and control.
Construction entities engaged in housing construction, municipal infrastructure construction, river course renovation, and building demolition, etc., shall report to the department responsible for the supervision and management of dust pollution prevention and control for recordation.
The construction entity shall set up hard enclosures at the construction site and take effective dust prevention and reduction measures such as covering, sectional operation, selective timing of construction, sprinkling water to suppress dust, and washing the ground and vehicles. Construction waste such as工程渣土 (engineering muck) and building earthwork shall be removed in a timely manner; if stored on site, they shall be covered with airtight dust-proof nets. Construction waste such as工程渣土 shall be treated for resource utilization.
The construction entity shall disclose information on dust pollution prevention and control measures, the person in charge, the supervisory department, etc. at the construction site.
For construction land that cannot be started for the time being, the construction unit shall cover the exposed ground; if it exceeds three months, it shall be greened, paved or covered.

Article 241: Vehicles and vessels transporting bulk or fluid materials such as coal, garbage, slag, sand, gravel, earth, and mortar shall adopt airtight or other effective measures to prevent material spillage causing dust pollution, and shall travel along prescribed routes.
Loading and unloading of materials shall adopt airtight or spray methods and other means to prevent dust pollution.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the management of cleaning and sweeping of roads, squares, parking lots, and other public places, promote clean power mechanized sweeping and other scientifically sound low-dust operation methods to prevent dust pollution.

Article 242: For municipal rivers and their banks, bare land on public land, and other bare land in cities and towns, the relevant departments shall, in accordance with the plans, organize the implementation of greening or permeable paving.

Article 243: Storage of coal, coal gangue, coal slag, coal ash, cement, lime, gypsum, sand, iron ore, and other materials prone to generating dust shall be enclosed; if enclosure is not possible, a tight enclosure at least as high as the stacked materials shall be erected, and effective covering measures shall be taken to prevent dust pollution.
Docks, mines, landfills, and disposal sites shall implement zoned operations and take effective measures to prevent dust pollution.
Article 244: It is prohibited to spray highly toxic or highly poisonous pesticides on trees, flowers, and grass in densely populated areas.

Article 245: People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments such as agriculture and rural affairs shall encourage and support the adoption of advanced applicable technologies for the comprehensive utilization of crop straw, fallen leaves, etc., through measures such as fertilizer, feed, energy, industrial raw materials, and edible fungus base material, and shall increase financial subsidies for agricultural machinery such as straw returning and integrated collection.
The people's governments at the county level shall organize the establishment and improvement of a service system for the collection, storage, transportation, disposal, and comprehensive utilization of crop straw, and shall use financial subsidies and other measures to support rural collective economic organizations, specialized farmer cooperatives, enterprises, etc., in providing services for the collection, storage, transportation, disposal, and comprehensive utilization of crop straw.

Article 246: Local people's governments at all levels shall scientifically and precisely strengthen the organization, guidance, and management of the burning of crop straw, fallen leaves, etc. It is prohibited to burn crop straw, fallen leaves, and other substances that produce smoke and dust pollution in the open air in densely populated areas, areas around airports, areas near main traffic lines, and other areas designated by people's governments at or above the provincial level, as well as during prescribed time periods.

Article 247: The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall, together with the competent department of health under the State Council, formulate and publish a list of toxic and hazardous air pollutants based on the degree of harm and impact of air pollutants on public health and the ecological environment, and shall update it in a timely manner, and implement risk management.
Enterprises and institutions that discharge the toxic and hazardous air pollutants listed in the list specified in the preceding paragraph shall, in accordance with state provisions, establish an environmental risk early warning system, conduct regular monitoring of discharge outlets and the surrounding environment, assess environmental risks, identify environmental safety hazards, and take effective measures to prevent environmental risks.

Article 248: Enterprises, institutions, and other producers and business operators that discharge persistent organic pollutants into the atmosphere, as well as operators of waste incineration facilities, shall, in accordance with state provisions, adopt technical methods and processes conducive to reducing emissions of persistent organic pollutants, and install effective purification devices to achieve compliance-based discharge.

Article 249: When formulating territorial spatial plans and related plans, people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall make integrated planning, rationally arrange land use and construction layout to prevent and reduce odor pollution.
If enterprises, institutions, and other producers and business operators generate malodorous gases during production and business operations, they shall scientifically select sites, set reasonable protective distances, and install purification devices or take other effective measures to prevent the discharge of malodorous gases.

Article 250: Local people's governments at all levels shall strengthen guidance on the layout and establishment of the catering service industry, and shall indicate the prohibited location requirements during the registration and licensing of business entities.
Catering service operators that discharge cooking fume pollutants shall install pollution prevention facilities such as cooking fume purification devices in accordance with regulations and shall maintain them in normal operation. It is prohibited to newly build, rebuild, or expand catering service projects that generate cooking fume, odor, or waste gas in residential buildings, commercial-residential mixed-use buildings without dedicated fume ducts, and commercial floors adjacent to residential floors within commercial-residential mixed-use buildings.
Catering service operators that discharge cooking fume pollutants shall take effective measures to ensure the discharge of pollutants meets the standards and to prevent pollution of the normal living environment of nearby residents.
No unit or individual shall barbecue food in the open air or provide venues for open-air barbecue food during the time periods or in areas prohibited by the local people's government.

Article 251: It is prohibited to burn asphalt, felt, rubber, plastic, leather, garbage, and other substances that produce toxic and hazardous smoke, dust, and malodorous gases in densely populated areas and other areas requiring special protection according to law.
It is prohibited to produce, sell, or set off fireworks and firecrackers that do not meet quality standards. No unit or individual shall set off fireworks and firecrackers during time periods or in areas prohibited by the local people's government at or above the county level.

Article 252: The State encourages and advocates civilized and green sacrificial practices.
Crematoria shall install pollution prevention facilities such as dust removal devices and maintain them in normal operation to prevent impacts on the surrounding environment.

Article 253: Operators engaged in service activities such as garment dry cleaning and motor vehicle maintenance shall, in accordance with relevant national standards or requirements, install pollution prevention facilities such as odor and waste gas treatment devices and maintain them in normal operation to prevent impacts on the surrounding environment.

Article 254: The State encourages and supports the production and use of substitutes for ozone-depleting substances, and shall gradually reduce and eventually cease the production and use of ozone-depleting substances.
The State implements total quantity control and quota management for the production, use, import, and export of ozone-depleting substances, and the specific measures shall be formulated by the State Council.

Article 255: The State shall establish and improve a joint prevention and control mechanism for air pollution in key areas, and shall overall coordinate the air pollution prevention and control work within key areas. The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall, based on the main functional area planning, the regional atmospheric environmental quality status, and the law of air pollution transmission and diffusion, designate national key areas for air pollution prevention and control, and shall report to the State Council for approval.
The people's governments of relevant provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government within the national key areas for air pollution prevention and control shall designate a lead local people's government, hold regular joint meetings, and carry out joint prevention and control of air pollution in accordance with the requirements of unified planning, unified standards, unified monitoring, and unified prevention measures, and shall implement the target responsibilities for air pollution prevention and control. The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall strengthen guidance and supervision.
Provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, by reference to the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article, designate key areas for air pollution prevention and control within their respective administrative regions.

Article 256: The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall, together with relevant departments and the people's governments of relevant provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government within national key areas for air pollution prevention and control, formulate joint prevention and control action plans for air pollution in key areas based on the socioeconomic development of the key areas and the carrying capacity of the atmospheric environment, clarify control targets, optimize regional economic layout, coordinate traffic management, develop clean and low-carbon energy, and propose key prevention tasks and measures to promote the improvement of atmospheric environmental quality in the key areas.

Article 257: The development and reform department under the State Council shall, together with the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council, further raise the requirements for pollution prevention, energy consumption, etc., in light of the actual industrial development and atmospheric environmental quality conditions of the national key areas for air pollution prevention and control.
The people's governments of relevant provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government within national key areas for air pollution prevention and control shall implement more stringent emission standards for air pollutants from motor vehicles, unify the inspection methods and emission limits for in-use motor vehicles, and supply qualified vehicle fuel in a supporting manner.

Article 258: When formulating plans for industrial parks, development zones, regional industries, and development that may cause serious pollution to the atmospheric environment of national key areas for air pollution prevention and control, the planning formulation authorities shall consult with the people's governments or relevant departments of the relevant provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government within the key areas.
If the construction of a project by a relevant province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government within a national key area for air pollution prevention and control may have a significant impact on the atmospheric environmental quality of an adjacent province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, the relevant information shall be promptly notified and consultation shall be carried out.
The consultation opinions and their adoption shall serve as important bases for the review or approval of the ecological environmental impact report or the ecological environmental impact report form.

Article 259: For newly built, rebuilt, or expanded coal-using projects within national key areas for air pollution prevention and control, equivalent or reduced substitution of coal shall be implemented.

Article 260: The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall organize the establishment and improvement of information sharing mechanisms for atmospheric environmental quality monitoring, air pollution source monitoring, and other related information in national key areas for air pollution prevention and control, shall use new technologies such as monitoring, simulation, satellite, aerial survey, and remote sensing to analyze the sources and changing trends of air pollution in the key areas, and shall make the information publicly available.

Article 261 The State shall establish and improve a monitoring and early warning system for heavily polluted weather.
The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council, together with the meteorological department and other relevant departments of the State Council, and the people's governments of the relevant provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government within key areas for the prevention and control of air pollution, shall establish and improve a mechanism for monitoring and early warning of heavily polluted weather in key areas and unify the classification standards for early warning. If heavily polluted regional weather may occur, timely notice shall be given to the people's governments of the relevant provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government within the key areas.
The competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts, together with the meteorological department and other relevant departments, shall establish and improve a mechanism for monitoring and early warning of heavily polluted weather within its administrative region.

Article 262 Local people's governments at or above the level of a city divided into districts and the people's governments of counties where heavily polluted weather may occur shall formulate contingency plans for heavy polluted weather, report them to the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at the next higher level for record, and make them public.

Article 263 The competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts, together with the competent meteorological authority, shall establish and improve a consultation mechanism to forecast atmospheric environmental quality. If heavily polluted weather may occur, a report shall be made in a timely manner to the people's government at the same level. The local people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts, based on the heavy polluted weather forecast information, shall conduct comprehensive assessment, determine the warning level, and issue a warning in a timely manner. The warning level shall be adjusted in a timely manner according to changes in circumstances. No unit or individual may release any heavy polluted weather forecast or warning information without authorization.
After the warning information is released, the people's government and its relevant departments shall, through television, radio, the internet, text messages, and other means, promptly inform the public to take health protection measures, guide the public in travel and adjustment of other related social activities.

Article 264 Local people's governments at or above the county level shall, based on the warning level of heavily polluted weather, promptly initiate the contingency plan, and may take such response measures as ordering relevant enterprises to suspend or limit production, restricting the operation of certain motor vehicles and the use of non-road mobile machinery, prohibiting fireworks and firecrackers, ceasing earthwork and building demolition operations at construction sites, ceasing outdoor barbecues, ceasing outdoor activities organized by kindergartens and schools, and organizing and carrying out weather modification operations, as needed for the response.
After the response is concluded, the people's government shall promptly conduct an assessment of the implementation of the contingency plan, and revise and improve the contingency plan as appropriate.

Article 265 The State shall strengthen the performance classification of key industries in heavily polluted weather. The level of performance classification shall serve as the basis for differentiated response measures for heavily polluted weather.
Book III Water Pollution Prevention and Control
Article 266 This Book applies to the prevention and control of pollution of surface water bodies such as rivers, lakes, canals, ditches, and reservoirs, as well as groundwater bodies.

Article 267 For the purposes of this Law, "water pollution" means the phenomenon in which the chemical, physical, biological, or radioactive properties of a water body are changed due to the introduction of certain substances, thereby affecting the effective use of water, endangering public health, or damaging the ecological environment, and causing deterioration of water quality.

Article 268 Water pollution prevention and control shall prioritize the protection of drinking water sources and ensure the safety of drinking water, strictly control industrial pollution and urban domestic pollution, prevent and control agricultural non-point source pollution, strengthen the establishment and management of sewage outlets into rivers, actively promote the construction of ecological treatment projects, and prevent, control, and reduce water environment pollution and ecological damage.

Article 269 The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall exercise unified supervision and administration over the national water pollution prevention and control work. The river basin ecological environment supervision and administration institution of the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall carry out relevant supervision and administration work on water pollution prevention and control within river basins according to law. The competent departments of ecological environment of local people's governments shall exercise unified supervision and administration over the water pollution prevention and control work within their respective administrative regions.
The maritime administration authority shall exercise supervision and administration over the prevention and control of pollution of waters by ships.
The water administrative, natural resources, health, housing and urban-rural construction, agriculture and rural affairs, fisheries and fishery administration, and other relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall exercise supervision and administration over the water pollution prevention and control work within their respective functions and duties.

Article 270 Water pollution prevention and control shall be planned uniformly by river basin or by region. The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council, together with the national development and reform, water administrative, and other relevant departments of the State Council, shall formulate the national river basin water ecological environment protection plan, specifying the ecological environment protection requirements for the Yangtze River, Yellow River, Huaihe River, Haihe River, Pearl River, Songhua River, Liaohe River, and other river basins, and submit it to the State Council for approval.
The river basin water ecological environment protection plan for rivers and lakes crossing counties within a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall be formulated by the competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government, together with the development and reform, water administrative, and other relevant departments, in accordance with the national river basin water ecological environment protection plan and local actual conditions, submitted to the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for approval, and reported to the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council for record.
Local people's governments at or above the county level may, based on the legally approved river basin water ecological environment protection plan and actual needs, organize the formulation of water ecological environment protection plans for their respective administrative regions.

Article 271 The relevant people's governments of cities divided into districts and counties shall, in accordance with the requirements of the water ecological environment quality improvement targets determined in the water ecological environment protection plan, formulate a time-bound compliance plan and take effective measures to achieve compliance within the prescribed period.
The relevant people's governments of cities divided into districts and counties shall report the time-bound compliance plan to the people's government at the next higher level for record.

Article 272 The State shall establish and improve a system for monitoring water ecological environment quality and monitoring water pollutant discharge. The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council, together with the water administrative department and other relevant departments of the State Council, shall organize a monitoring network, uniformly plan the establishment of national water ecological environment quality monitoring stations, establish and improve a mechanism for sharing monitoring data, and strengthen the management of water ecological environment monitoring.

Article 273 The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council and its river basin ecological environment supervision and administration institutions shall be responsible for monitoring the water ecological environment quality of water bodies at provincial boundaries.

Article 274 The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council, together with the competent health department of the State Council, shall, based on the degree of harm and impact on public health and the ecological environment, formulate and publish a list of toxic and hazardous water pollutants and update it in a timely manner, implementing risk management.
Enterprise and public institutions and other producers and business operators that discharge toxic and hazardous water pollutants listed in the list provided in the preceding paragraph shall monitor the discharge outlets and the surrounding environment, assess environmental risks, investigate and eliminate environmental safety hazards, disclose information on toxic and hazardous water pollutants to the public, and take effective measures to prevent environmental risks.

Article 275 The establishment, alteration, or expansion of a sewage outlet into a river shall, in accordance with the provisions, be reported to and obtain consent from the competent ecological environment department with jurisdiction or the river basin ecological environment supervision and administration institution of the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council. If the establishment, alteration, or expansion of a sewage outlet into a river may affect flood control, water supply, dike safety, or river regime stability, the opinions of the water administrative department of the local people's government or the relevant river basin management institution shall be solicited during the approval. The specific measures for the establishment and management of sewage outlets into rivers shall be formulated by the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council.
For the purposes of this Law, "sewage outlet into a river" means an outfall that directly or through pipelines, ditches, canals, or other discharge channels discharges sewage into water bodies such as rivers, lakes, canals, and reservoirs.

Article 276 In water function areas where water ecological environment quality does not meet the standards, except for sewage outlets into rivers for important livelihood projects such as centralized urban and rural sewage treatment facilities, the establishment, alteration, or expansion of sewage outlets into rivers shall be strictly controlled.

Article 277 Local people's governments at or above the county level shall organize investigations and remediation of sewage outlets into rivers within their respective administrative regions, clarify the responsible entities, and implement classified management.
The responsible entity of a sewage outlet into a river shall strengthen source control, patrol and maintain discharge channels, and carry out remediation, standardized construction, and maintenance management of the sewage outlet into a river.

Article 278 Where multiple units and individuals share a sewage outlet into a river, the responsible entity shall strengthen monitoring of the sewage outlet into a river, and conduct surveillance and automatic monitoring in accordance with the provisions.

Article 279 It is prohibited to discharge oils, acid liquids, alkaline liquids, or highly toxic waste liquids into water bodies. It is prohibited to wash vehicles and containers that have stored oils or toxic and hazardous pollutants in water bodies.
It is prohibited to discharge or dump radioactive solid waste or wastewater containing high- and medium-level radioactive substances into water bodies. The discharge of wastewater containing low-level radioactive substances into water bodies shall comply with the state's provisions and standards on the prevention and control of radioactive pollution.

Article 280 The discharge of thermal wastewater into water bodies shall be subject to effective measures to ensure that the water temperature of the water body meets the water ecological environment quality standards, and to avoid causing harm to rare and endangered aquatic organisms and aquatic resources.
Article 281 Wastewater containing pathogens shall be disinfected and, after meeting relevant national standards, may be discharged.

Article 282 No industrial waste residue, urban garbage, or other wastes shall be discharged or dumped into waters.
No soluble highly toxic waste residue containing mercury, cadmium, arsenic, chromium, lead, cyanide, yellow phosphorus, or the like shall be discharged or dumped into waters or directly buried underground.
For places where soluble highly toxic waste residues are stored, measures shall be taken to prevent water seepage, leakage, and loss.

Article 283 Local people's governments at all levels shall organize the investigation and treatment of black and odorous water bodies within their respective administrative areas, establish and improve long-term mechanisms, formulate and publish lists of black and odorous water bodies, scientifically formulate treatment plans for black and odorous water bodies, and systematically promote the remediation of such water bodies to prevent them from becoming black and odorous again.

Article 284 People's governments at or above the county level shall organize the relevant departments of water administration, natural resources, ecological environment, and others to conduct investigation and assessment of groundwater conditions, including investigation and assessment of groundwater resources, groundwater pollution, and hydrogeological survey and assessment.
The conclusions of groundwater condition investigation and assessment shall serve as important bases for formulating plans for the protection, utilization, and pollution prevention of groundwater, as well as for managing groundwater, and shall be disclosed to the public according to law.

Article 285 The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall, together with the relevant departments of water administration, natural resources, and others under the State Council, guide the nationwide work on delineating key areas for groundwater pollution prevention and control.
The competent department of ecological environment of a provincial people's government shall, together with the relevant departments of water administration, natural resources, and others, delineate key areas for groundwater pollution prevention and control in light of the needs of such prevention and control in its administrative area, and specify management requirements for environmental access, hidden danger investigation, risk control, and the like.

Article 286 No construction project that may cause groundwater pollution shall be newly built, reconstructed, or expanded within the protection scope of spring areas and in areas with strong karst development, where there are many sinkholes and karst funnels.

Article 287 The operation and management units of chemical industry parks, chemical projects, mining areas, tailings ponds, hazardous waste disposal sites, and landfill sites shall take measures such as anti-leakage measures and construct groundwater quality monitoring wells to monitor and prevent groundwater pollution.
Underground oil tanks at gas stations, oil extraction plants, and the like shall use double-layer tanks or take other effective measures such as building anti-leakage pools, and shall be monitored for leakage prevention to prevent groundwater pollution.
No wastewater containing toxic and harmful pollutants, wastewater containing pathogens, or other wastes shall be transported or stored in ditches, pits, and ponds without anti-leakage measures.

Article 288 The exploitation of multiple aquifers and the recharge of groundwater shall prevent cross-aquifer pollution.
Where there is a significant difference in water quality among the aquifers of multi-layer groundwater, layered exploitation shall be carried out; the already polluted phreatic water and confined water shall not be exploited by mixing.

Article 289 For the construction of underground engineering facilities or the conduct of underground exploration, mining, and other activities, protective measures shall be taken to prevent groundwater pollution.
Abandoned mines, drill holes, or water intake wells shall be sealed or backfilled.
Article 290 Artificial recharge to replenish groundwater shall comply with relevant water quality standards and shall not degrade the quality of groundwater.

Article 291 Enterprises and public institutions that may cause water pollution accidents shall formulate emergency response plans for such accidents, make emergency preparations, and conduct regular drills.
Enterprises and public institutions that produce or store hazardous chemicals shall take measures such as sealing, containment, and transfer to prevent the direct discharge into waters of fire-fighting waste generated in the process of handling production safety accidents, which may seriously pollute water bodies.

Article 292 Where an accident or other emergency occurs in an enterprise or public institution, causing or possibly causing a water pollution accident, it shall immediately activate its emergency response plan, take emergency measures such as isolation to prevent water pollutants from entering waters, and report to the local people's government at or above the county level or the competent department of ecological environment at the place where the accident occurs. Upon receiving the report, the competent department of ecological environment shall promptly report to the people's government at the same level and send a copy to the relevant departments such as the water administration and emergency management.
Where a fishery pollution accident is caused or a water pollution accident is caused by a fishing vessel, it shall be reported to the competent department of fisheries and fishery administration at the place where the accident occurs for investigation and handling. Where a water pollution accident is caused by other vessels, it shall be reported to the maritime administrative agency at the place where the accident occurs for investigation and handling; if damage is caused to fisheries, the maritime administrative agency shall notify the competent department of fisheries and fishery administration to participate in the investigation and handling.

Article 293 The people's governments of cities divided into districts and of counties shall organize the formulation of emergency response plans for drinking water safety emergencies.
Drinking water supply units shall, in accordance with the local emergency response plans for drinking water safety emergencies, formulate corresponding emergency response plans, report them to the people's governments of the cities divided into districts or counties for filing, and conduct regular drills.
Where a water pollution accident occurs in a drinking water source or other emergencies that may affect drinking water safety occur, the drinking water supply unit shall take emergency measures, report to the local people's government of the city divided into districts or county, and disclose the information to the public. The relevant people's government shall promptly activate the emergency response plan based on the actual situation and take effective measures to ensure the safety of water supply.
