Where the pollutant content exceeds the soil pollution risk control standards, the soil pollution status investigation report shall also include the type of pollution, the source of pollution, and whether the groundwater is polluted.

Article 433 Risk control and remediation activities shall be carried out in accordance with local conditions, in a scientific and reasonable manner, and with enhanced pertinence and effectiveness.
Risk control and remediation activities shall not cause new pollution to the soil and the surrounding environment.

Article 434 Before implementing risk control and remediation activities, the relevant departments of the local people's government shall have the right, based on the actual circumstances, to require the soil pollution liability holder and the land use right holder to take measures such as removing the pollution source and preventing the spread of pollution.

Article 435 Wastewater, waste gas and solid waste generated during risk control and remediation activities shall be treated and disposed of according to the provisions, and shall meet the relevant ecological and environmental protection standards.
Where the solid waste generated during risk control and remediation activities and the dismantled facilities, equipment or buildings and structures constitute hazardous waste, they shall be disposed of in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the requirements of relevant standards.
During the remediation construction period, a bulletin board shall be set up to disclose the relevant information and ecological and environmental protection measures to the public.

Article 436 Where a remediation construction unit transports contaminated soil, it shall formulate a transport plan and submit in advance to the competent departments of ecology and environment in the locality and the receiving locality the transport time, method and route, the quantity, destination and final disposal measures of the contaminated soil, etc.
Where the transported contaminated soil constitutes hazardous waste, the remediation construction unit shall dispose of it in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the requirements of relevant standards.

Article 437 When conducting an assessment of risk control effectiveness or an assessment of remediation effectiveness, an effectiveness assessment report shall be prepared.
The effectiveness assessment report shall mainly include whether the risk control and remediation objectives determined in the soil pollution risk assessment report have been achieved, etc.
Where post-management is required after the completion of risk control and remediation activities, the soil pollution liability holder shall implement post-management as required.

Article 438 Entities engaged in activities such as soil pollution status investigation, soil pollution risk assessment, risk control, remediation, assessment of risk control effectiveness, assessment of remediation effectiveness, and post-management shall have corresponding professional capabilities.
Entities entrusted to engage in the activities mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall be responsible for the authenticity, accuracy and completeness of the investigation reports, risk assessment reports, risk control effectiveness assessment reports and remediation effectiveness assessment reports they issue, and shall be responsible for the results of risk control, remediation, post-management and other activities in accordance with the agreement.

Article 439 The soil pollution liability holder has the obligation to implement risk control and remediation of soil pollution. Where the soil pollution liability holder cannot be identified, the land use right holder shall implement the risk control and remediation of soil pollution.
Local people's governments and their relevant departments may, based on actual circumstances, organize the implementation of risk control and remediation of soil pollution.
The State encourages and supports relevant parties to voluntarily implement risk control and remediation of soil pollution.

Article 440 The expenses incurred from implementing or organizing the implementation of activities such as soil pollution status investigation, soil pollution risk assessment, risk control, remediation, assessment of risk control effectiveness, assessment of remediation effectiveness, and post-management shall be borne by the soil pollution liability holder.

Article 441 Where the person liable for soil contamination changes, the entity or individual that succeeds to its/his/her claims and debts after the change shall perform the relevant obligations of soil contamination risk control and remediation and bear the relevant costs.

Article 442 Where the person liable for soil contamination is unclear or disputed, for agricultural land, the competent departments of agricultural and rural affairs and of forestry and grassland of the local people's government shall, jointly with the competent departments of ecological environment and of natural resources, make the determination; for construction land, the competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government shall, jointly with the competent department of natural resources, make the determination. The determination measures shall be formulated by the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council jointly with the relevant departments.

Article 443 Where an emergency occurs that may cause soil contamination, the local people's government and its relevant departments, and the relevant enterprises, public institutions, and other producers and business operators shall immediately take emergency measures to prevent soil contamination, and shall, in accordance with the provisions of this Law, properly conduct soil contamination status monitoring, investigation, soil contamination risk assessment, risk control, and remediation.

Article 444 The State shall establish and improve a classified management system for agricultural land. According to the degree of soil contamination and relevant standards, agricultural land shall be classified into priority protection class, safe utilization class, and strict control class.

Article 445 The local people's government at or above the county level shall, according to law, designate eligible priority protection class farmland as permanent basic farmland and implement strict protection.
No construction project that may cause soil contamination shall be newly built in the concentrated area of permanent basic farmland; those already built shall be demolished or closed within a specified time limit.

Article 446 Where unused land, reclaimed land, or the like is to be cultivated, the competent department of agricultural and rural affairs of the local people's government shall, jointly with the competent departments of ecological environment and of natural resources, conduct a soil contamination status investigation and implement classified management according to law.

Article 447 For agricultural land plots where the general survey, detailed survey, monitoring, and on-site inspection of soil contamination status indicate a risk of soil contamination, the competent departments of agricultural and rural affairs and of forestry and grassland of the local people's government shall, jointly with the competent departments of ecological environment and of natural resources, conduct a soil contamination status investigation.
For agricultural land plots where the soil contamination status investigation shows that the pollutant content exceeds the soil contamination risk control standard, the competent departments of agricultural and rural affairs and of forestry and grassland of the local people's government shall, jointly with the competent departments of ecological environment and of natural resources, organize a soil contamination risk assessment and manage them in accordance with the classified management system for agricultural land.

Article 450 Where soil contamination of agricultural land plots of safe utilization class or strict control class affects or may affect the safety of groundwater or drinking water sources, the competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government shall, jointly with the relevant departments such as agriculture and rural affairs, forestry and grassland, formulate a pollution prevention plan and take corresponding measures.

Article 451 For agricultural land plots of safe utilization class or strict control class, the person liable for soil contamination shall, in accordance with the national provisions and the requirements of the soil contamination risk assessment report, take corresponding risk control measures and periodically report to the competent departments of agricultural and rural affairs and of forestry and grassland of the local people's government.

Article 452 For agricultural land plots where the pollutant content of the output agricultural products exceeds the standard and remediation is required, the person liable for soil contamination shall prepare a remediation plan, report it to the competent departments of agricultural and rural affairs and of forestry and grassland of the local people's government for record, and implement it. The remediation plan shall include measures for the prevention and control of groundwater contamination.
Remediation activities shall give priority to bioremediation measures that do not affect agricultural production or reduce soil production functions, so as to block or reduce the entry of pollutants into the edible parts of crops and ensure the quality and safety of agricultural products.
After the completion of risk control and remediation activities, the person liable for soil contamination shall separately entrust a relevant entity to assess the effectiveness of risk control and remediation, and submit the effectiveness assessment report to the competent departments of agricultural and rural affairs and of forestry and grassland of the local people's government for record.
Rural collective economic organizations and their members, farmer specialized cooperatives, and other agricultural production and business entities shall have the obligation to assist in implementing soil contamination risk control and remediation.

Article 453 The State shall implement a system of a list for risk control and remediation of soil contamination on construction land.
The list for risk control and remediation of soil contamination on construction land shall be formulated by the competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government jointly with the relevant departments such as natural resources, shall be disclosed to the public in accordance with the provisions, and shall be updated in a timely manner based on the status of risk control and remediation.

Article 454 For construction land plots where the general survey, detailed survey, monitoring, and on-site inspection of soil contamination status indicate a risk of soil contamination, the competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government shall require the land use right holder to conduct a soil contamination status investigation in accordance with the provisions.
Where the use of land is changed to residential, public administration, or public service land, a soil contamination status investigation shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions before the change. The soil contamination status investigation shall be completed within the time limit determined by the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.
The soil contamination status investigation reports specified in the preceding two paragraphs shall be submitted to the competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government, which shall organize an evaluation jointly with the competent department of natural resources.

Article 455 For construction land plots where the evaluation of the soil contamination status investigation report shows that the pollutant content exceeds the soil contamination risk control standard, the person liable for soil contamination and the land use right holder shall conduct a soil contamination risk assessment in accordance with the provisions of the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council, and submit the soil contamination risk assessment report to the competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government.

Article 456 The competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government shall, jointly with the relevant departments such as natural resources, organize an evaluation of the soil contamination risk assessment report in accordance with the provisions of the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council, promptly include the plots that require risk control and remediation into the list for risk control and remediation of soil contamination on construction land, and periodically report to the competent departments of ecological environment and of natural resources of the State Council.
Plots included in the list for risk control and remediation of soil contamination on construction land shall not be used as residential, public administration, or public service land. Specific management measures shall be formulated by the provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government.

Article 457 For plots in the list for risk control and remediation of soil contamination on construction land, the person liable for soil contamination shall, in accordance with the national provisions and the requirements of the soil contamination risk assessment report, take corresponding risk control measures and periodically report to the competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government. The risk control measures shall include measures for the prevention and control of groundwater contamination.

Article 459 For plots in the list for risk control and remediation of soil contamination on construction land that require remediation, the person liable for soil contamination shall prepare a remediation plan in light of the territorial space planning, report it to the competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government for record, and implement it. The remediation plan shall include measures for the prevention and control of groundwater contamination.

Article 460 After the completion of risk control and remediation activities, the person liable for soil contamination shall separately entrust a relevant entity to assess the effectiveness of risk control and remediation, and submit the effectiveness assessment report to the competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government for record.

Article 461 For a plot of land for construction use that meets the risk control and remediation targets specified in the soil pollution risk assessment report, the soil pollution liable party or the land use right holder may apply to the competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government to remove the plot from the list of land for construction use subject to soil pollution risk control and remediation.
The competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government shall, in conjunction with the natural resources department and other relevant departments, organize a review of the risk control effectiveness assessment report and the remediation effectiveness assessment report, and shall promptly remove from the list of land for construction use subject to soil pollution risk control and remediation those plots that have met the risk control and remediation targets specified in the soil pollution risk assessment report and can be safely used, disclose such information to the public in accordance with the relevant provisions, and periodically report to the competent department of ecological environment and the competent department of natural resources of the State Council.
For a plot of land for construction use that has not met the risk control and remediation targets specified in the soil pollution risk assessment report, or for which the soil pollution status investigation, soil pollution risk assessment, risk control, remediation, risk control effectiveness assessment, or remediation effectiveness assessment has not been conducted in accordance with the relevant provisions, no project unrelated to risk control or remediation may commence construction; if construction has already commenced, the construction shall be immediately stopped.

Article 462 Prior to the change in use of the production and operation land of a key entity under supervision for soil pollution, or prior to the recovery or transfer of its land use right, the land use right holder shall conduct a soil pollution status investigation in accordance with the relevant provisions. The soil pollution status investigation report shall be submitted to the immovable property registration authority of the local people's government as immovable property registration materials, and shall be filed with the competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government; if the land use right holder fails to submit the soil pollution status investigation report, the immovable property registration authority of the local people's government shall require him to provide it.

Article 463 Where the land use right has been recovered by the local people's government and the soil pollution liable party is the former land use right holder, the local people's government shall organize the implementation of soil pollution risk control and remediation.
Division 6 Prevention and Control of Solid Waste Pollution
Article 464 This Division applies to the prevention and control of solid waste pollution.

Article 465 For the purposes of this Law, "solid waste" means articles and substances that are generated in production, daily life, and other activities and have lost their original use value, or although they have not lost their use value, have been discarded or abandoned, including solid, semi-solid, and gaseous articles and substances placed in containers, as well as articles and substances that are included in the management of solid waste under laws and administrative regulations. Excluded are those that, after harmless processing and treatment and that meet mandatory national product quality standards, do not endanger public health or ecological safety, or are determined not to be solid waste according to solid waste identification standards and procedures.

Article 466 The prevention and control of solid waste pollution shall adhere to the principles of reduction, resource utilization, and harmlessness, and strengthen the management and control of the entire process of generation, collection, storage, transportation, utilization, and disposal.

Article 467 The State shall take effective measures to strengthen the comprehensive management of solid waste, promote source reduction and full resource utilization of solid waste in urban and rural areas, and minimize the amount of solid waste disposed of by landfill.
Any unit or individual shall take effective measures to reduce the generation of solid waste, promote the comprehensive utilization of solid waste, and reduce the hazardous nature of solid waste.

Article 468 Units and individuals that generate, collect, store, transport, utilize, or dispose of solid waste shall take effective measures to prevent or reduce solid waste pollution and bear liability for the pollution caused according to law.
"Storage of solid waste" means the activity of temporarily placing solid waste in specific facilities or premises.
"Utilization of solid waste" means the activity of directly using solid waste as substitute raw materials or fuel, or extracting substances from solid waste as raw materials or fuel.
"Disposal of solid waste" means the activity of incinerating solid waste or using other methods to change the physical, chemical, or biological characteristics of solid waste, so as to reduce the quantity of generated solid waste, reduce the volume of solid waste, or reduce or eliminate its hazardous components, or the activity of ultimately placing solid waste in a landfill that meets the requirements of ecological and environmental protection.

Article 469 The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall exercise unified supervision and administration over the prevention and control of solid waste pollution nationwide. The competent departments of ecological environment of local people's governments shall exercise unified supervision and administration over the prevention and control of solid waste pollution within their respective administrative regions.
The competent departments of development and reform, industry and information technology, natural resources, housing and urban-rural construction, transportation, agriculture and rural affairs, commerce, health, customs, and other relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall exercise supervision and administration over the prevention and control of solid waste pollution within the scope of their respective duties.

Article 470 Provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, through consultation, establish a joint prevention and control mechanism for solid waste pollution across administrative regions, and coordinate the planning, facility construction, and solid waste transfer, among other tasks.

Article 471 Local people's governments at or above the city level with districts shall formulate plans for the prevention and control of solid waste pollution, and coordinate the planning and construction of facilities and premises for solid waste transfer, centralized disposal, among others, so as to advance the work of preventing and controlling solid waste pollution.

Article 472 The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall, in conjunction with the relevant departments, formulate solid waste identification standards, identification procedures, technical standards for pollution prevention and control, and control standards for the content of toxic and hazardous substances in industrial solid waste, based on the national ecological environment quality standards and the national economic and technical conditions.

Article 473 Standards for the comprehensive utilization of solid waste shall specify the limits for toxic and hazardous substances in the products of comprehensive utilization.
The comprehensive utilization of solid waste shall comply with the provisions of ecological and environmental laws and regulations, and meet the comprehensive utilization standards for solid waste and the technical standards for pollution prevention and control. The use of products from the comprehensive utilization of solid waste shall conform to the purposes and standards prescribed by the State.

Article 474 The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall, in conjunction with the relevant departments, establish a national information platform for the prevention and control of pollution from hazardous waste and other solid waste, and promote the whole-process monitoring and information-based traceability of the generation, collection, storage, transfer, utilization, and disposal of solid waste.

Article 475 Units and other business operators that generate, collect, store, transport, utilize, or dispose of solid waste shall take measures to prevent scattering, loss, leakage, or other measures to prevent environmental pollution, and shall not dump, pile up, discard, scatter, spill, or incinerate solid waste without authorization.

Article 476 Where solid waste is to be transferred out of the administrative region of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for storage or disposal, an application shall be submitted to the competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government of the place where the solid waste is transferred from. The competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government of the place of origin shall, after promptly consulting with and obtaining the consent of the competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government of the place of acceptance, approve the transfer of the solid waste out of the administrative region of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government within the prescribed time limit. Without approval, no transfer may be made.
Where solid waste is transferred out of the administrative region of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for utilization, the relevant information shall be submitted in advance to the competent departments of ecological environment of the provincial people's governments of both the place of origin and the place of acceptance through the solid waste pollution prevention and control information platform or other means.
Article 477 Solid waste from outside the territory of the People's Republic of China is prohibited from being dumped, piled up, or disposed of within the territory.

Article 478 The State implements a zero import policy for solid waste, and the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall, in conjunction with the competent departments of commerce, development and reform, customs, and other relevant departments of the State Council, organize its implementation.

Article 479 Where the customs discovers that imported goods are suspected of being solid waste, it may entrust a professional institution to conduct attribute identification, and shall manage them according to law based on the identification conclusion.

Article 480 Units and other business operators that collect, store, transport, utilize, or dispose of solid waste shall strengthen the management and maintenance of relevant facilities, equipment, and premises, and ensure their normal operation and use.

Article 481 Within ecological protection red line areas, permanent basic farmland concentrated areas, and other areas requiring special protection, the construction of facilities and sites for centralized storage, utilization, and disposal of industrial solid waste, construction waste, and hazardous waste, as well as landfill sites for domestic waste, is prohibited.

Article 482 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall, when formulating territorial space plans and relevant plans, take into overall consideration the demand for the construction of facilities and sites for the transfer and centralized disposal of solid waste such as domestic waste, construction waste, and hazardous waste, and shall guarantee the land for such facilities and sites.

Article 484 Entities that collect, store, transport, utilize, or dispose of hazardous waste shall, in accordance with the provisions, take out compulsory environmental pollution liability insurance. The specific implementation measures for the compulsory environmental pollution liability insurance system shall be formulated by the financial regulatory authority under the State Council jointly with the competent ecological environment department under the State Council.

Article 485 The competent ecological environment department of the people's government of a city divided into districts, jointly with the relevant departments of housing and urban-rural development, agriculture and rural affairs, and health, shall periodically disclose to the public information on the types, quantities, disposal capacity, and status of utilization and disposal of solid waste.
Entities that generate, collect, store, transport, utilize, or dispose of solid waste shall, in accordance with law, promptly disclose to the public information on the prevention and control of solid waste pollution and accept public supervision.
Entities that utilize or dispose of solid waste shall, in accordance with law, open their facilities and sites to the public to enhance public awareness of ecological and environmental protection and public participation.

Article 486 The prevention and control of pollution of the marine environment by solid waste and the prevention and control of pollution by radioactive solid waste shall not be governed by this Subchapter.
The prevention and control of pollution by liquid waste shall be governed by this Subchapter, except that the prevention and control of pollution by wastewater discharged into water bodies shall not be governed by this Subchapter.

Article 487 The competent ecological environment department under the State Council, jointly with the relevant departments such as the development and reform department and the industry and information technology department under the State Council, shall define the extent of harm and impact of industrial solid waste on public health and the ecological environment, formulate technical policies for the prevention and control of industrial solid waste pollution, and organize the promotion of advanced production processes and equipment for the prevention and control of industrial solid waste pollution.
For the purposes of this Law, "industrial solid waste" means solid waste generated in industrial production activities.

Article 488 The competent industry and information technology department under the State Council, jointly with the relevant departments, shall organize the research, development, and promotion of production processes and equipment that reduce the generation and harmfulness of industrial solid waste, and shall formulate and announce a list of outdated production processes and equipment that generate industrial solid waste causing serious environmental pollution and are subject to elimination within a specified time limit.
Producers, importers, sellers, and users shall, within the time limit prescribed by the competent industry and information technology department under the State Council jointly with the relevant departments, cease the production, import, sale, or use of the equipment listed in the list provided in the preceding paragraph. Persons using the production processes shall, within the time limit prescribed by the competent industry and information technology department under the State Council jointly with the relevant departments, cease the use of the production processes listed in the list provided in the preceding paragraph.
Equipment listed in the elimination list that has been eliminated shall not be transferred to others for use.

Article 489 Entities that generate industrial solid waste shall establish and improve a responsibility system for pollution prevention and control covering the entire process of generation, collection, storage, transportation, utilization, and disposal of industrial solid waste, shall establish management records for industrial solid waste, truthfully record information such as the types, quantities, flow directions, storage, utilization, and disposal of industrial solid waste, so as to achieve traceability and inquiry of industrial solid waste, and shall adopt measures to prevent pollution by industrial solid waste.
It is prohibited to place industrial solid waste into domestic waste collection facilities.

Article 490 Where an entity that generates industrial solid waste entrusts another person with the transportation, utilization, or disposal of industrial solid waste, it shall verify the principal qualification and technical capability of the entrusted party, enter into a written contract in accordance with law, and specify in the contract the pollution prevention and control requirements.
The entrusted party, when transporting, utilizing, or disposing of industrial solid waste, shall fulfill the pollution prevention and control requirements in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the contract, and shall inform the entity that generated the industrial solid waste of the transportation, utilization, and disposal status.

Article 491 The pollution discharge permit of an entity that generates industrial solid waste and is subject to pollution discharge permit management shall record information such as the requirements for the storage, utilization, and disposal of industrial solid waste.

Article 492 An entity that generates industrial solid waste shall provide the competent ecological environment department of the locality with relevant information such as the types, quantities, flow directions, storage, utilization, and disposal of industrial solid waste, as well as specific measures for reducing the generation of industrial solid waste and promoting comprehensive utilization.

Article 493 Entities that generate, store, utilize, or dispose of industrial solid waste shall, in accordance with national provisions, conduct testing and monitoring of industrial solid waste, and shall take necessary measures in accordance with classified management requirements to prevent pollution by industrial solid waste.

Article 494 An entity that generates industrial solid waste shall, based on economic and technological conditions, utilize the industrial solid waste; where it is temporarily not utilized or cannot be utilized, it shall, in accordance with the provisions of the competent ecological environment department under the State Council and other relevant departments, construct storage facilities and sites, store them safely by classification, or adopt harmless disposal measures. The storage of industrial solid waste shall adopt protective measures that meet national ecological environmental protection standards.
The construction of facilities and sites for the storage and disposal of industrial solid waste shall meet national ecological environmental protection standards.

Article 495 Where an entity that generates industrial solid waste is terminated, it shall, before termination, adopt pollution prevention and control measures for the facilities and sites for the storage and disposal of industrial solid waste, and shall properly dispose of the industrial solid waste that has not been disposed of, so as to prevent environmental pollution.
Where an entity that generates industrial solid waste undergoes a change, the entity after the change shall, in accordance with the relevant national provisions on ecological and environmental protection, safely dispose of the industrial solid waste that has not been disposed of and its storage and disposal facilities and sites, or take effective measures to ensure the safe operation of such facilities and sites. Where the parties before the change have otherwise agreed on the responsibility for pollution prevention and control of industrial solid waste and its storage and disposal facilities and sites, such agreement shall prevail. However, the parties shall not be exempted from the obligation of pollution prevention and control.

Article 496 The exploration and mining of mineral resources shall adopt exploration and mining methods and process technologies that are conducive to protecting the ecological environment and preventing pollution by solid waste, and shall reduce the generation and storage of mining solid waste such as tailings, coal gangue, and waste rock.
After the cessation of use of storage facilities for mining solid waste such as tailings, coal gangue, and waste rock, mining enterprises shall, in accordance with the relevant national provisions on ecological and environmental protection, carry out closure to prevent environmental pollution and ecological damage.

Article 497 The prevention and control of pollution of tailings storage facilities shall be subject to graded and classified management.
The operation and management units of tailings storage facilities shall establish a system for investigating and controlling environmental pollution hazards, and shall regularly carry out investigations of environmental pollution hazards to prevent environmental pollution.
Article 498 The State encourages the adoption of advanced process technologies for the comprehensive utilization of mining solid waste such as tailings, coal gangue, and waste rock.

Article 499 The State promotes the system of domestic waste classification.
The classification of domestic waste adheres to the principles of government promotion, universal participation, urban-rural coordination, adaptation to local conditions, and simplicity and convenience.
For the purposes of this Law, "domestic waste" means solid waste generated in daily life or in activities providing services for daily life, as well as solid waste that laws and administrative regulations stipulate to be treated as domestic waste.

Article 500 Local people's governments at or above the county level shall accelerate the establishment and improvement of a domestic waste management system for categorized delivery, categorized collection, categorized transportation, and categorized treatment, so as to achieve effective coverage of the domestic waste classification system.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall establish and improve a coordination mechanism for domestic waste classification work, and strengthen and coordinate the capacity building for domestic waste classification management.
People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall organize the promotion of domestic waste classification, educate and guide the public to develop the habit of domestic waste classification, and supervise and guide the work of domestic waste classification.

Article 501 The relevant departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions and duties, strengthen the management of production and circulation of products, avoid excessive packaging, organize the marketing of clean vegetables, and reduce the amount of domestic waste generated.

Article 502 People's governments at or above the county level shall make overall arrangements for the construction of facilities and sites for the collection, transportation, and treatment of domestic waste in urban and rural areas, determine the locations of such facilities and sites, improve the level of comprehensive utilization and harmless disposal of domestic waste, promote the industrialization of domestic waste collection and treatment, and gradually establish a sound social service system for the prevention and control of domestic waste pollution.

Article 503 Local people's governments at all levels shall strengthen the prevention and control of domestic waste pollution in rural areas, protect and improve the rural living environment.
The State encourages source reduction of rural domestic waste. In urban-rural fringe areas, densely populated rural areas, and other places where conditions permit, an integrated urban-rural domestic waste management system shall be established; in other rural areas, domestic waste management models shall be actively explored, and domestic waste shall be utilized nearby or on site or disposed of properly in light of local conditions.

Article 504 The competent department of environmental sanitation of the people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts shall formulate specifications for the construction and operation of facilities and sites for the sweeping, collection, storage, transportation, and treatment of domestic waste, publish a guidance catalog for the classification of domestic waste, and strengthen supervision and management.

Article 505 The environmental sanitation department and other relevant departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions and duties, organize the sweeping, collection, transportation, and treatment of urban and rural domestic waste, and may select qualified units to engage in the sweeping, collection, transportation, and treatment of domestic waste through means such as bidding.

Article 506 Units, households, and individuals that generate domestic waste shall, according to law, fulfill the obligations of source reduction and classified disposal of domestic waste, and bear the responsibilities of domestic waste generators.
Any unit or individual shall, according to law, sort and deposit domestic waste at designated places. It is prohibited to arbitrarily dump, pile, discard, scatter, spill, or burn domestic waste.
Government organs, public institutions, etc. shall play an exemplary and leading role in the classification of domestic waste.
Domestic waste that has been sorted and deposited shall be collected, transported, and treated by category in accordance with the provisions.

Article 507 The sweeping, collection, transportation, and treatment of urban and rural domestic waste shall comply with the state provisions on ecological and environmental protection and environmental sanitation management to prevent environmental pollution.
Hazardous waste that is sorted and collected separately from domestic waste and falls under the category of hazardous waste shall be managed as hazardous waste.
Article 508 Business units engaged in public transportation shall promptly sweep and collect domestic waste generated during transportation.

Article 509 Farmers' markets, agricultural product wholesale markets, etc. shall strengthen environmental sanitation management, keep the environment clean and sanitary, and promptly sweep, sort, collect, and properly dispose of the garbage generated.

Article 510 Units engaged in the development of new urban areas, reconstruction of old districts, development and construction of residential communities, and construction of villages and towns, as well as units that operate and manage public facilities and places such as airports, docks, stations, parks, shopping malls, and stadiums, shall, in accordance with the state provisions on environmental sanitation, construct supporting domestic waste collection facilities.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall coordinate the effective connection between public domestic waste transfer and treatment facilities and the collection facilities specified in the preceding paragraph, and strengthen the integration of the classified domestic waste collection and transportation system and the renewable resource recovery system in terms of planning, construction, and operation.

Article 511 Substances recovered from domestic waste shall be used in accordance with the purposes and standards prescribed by the state, and shall not be used for producing products that may endanger human health.

Article 512 The construction of domestic waste treatment facilities and sites shall comply with the ecological and environmental protection and environmental sanitation standards prescribed by the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council and the competent department of housing and urban-rural development of the State Council.
Adjacent areas are encouraged to make overall arrangements for the construction of domestic waste treatment facilities and promote the cross-administrative-region co-construction and sharing of domestic waste treatment facilities.
It is prohibited to close, idle, or dismantle domestic waste treatment facilities or sites without authorization; where it is genuinely necessary to close, idle, or dismantle them, approval shall be obtained from the environmental sanitation department of the local people's government at the city divided into districts or county level after consultation with the local competent department of ecological environment, and measures shall be taken to prevent environmental pollution.

Article 513 Domestic waste treatment units shall, in accordance with the state provisions, install and use monitoring equipment to monitor the discharge of pollutants in real time and disclose pollutant discharge data to the public in real time. The monitoring equipment shall be networked with the monitoring equipment of the local competent department of ecological environment.

Article 514 The environmental sanitation department of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for organizing the resource utilization and harmless treatment of kitchen waste.
Units and other producers and business operators that generate or collect kitchen waste shall deliver the kitchen waste to units with corresponding qualifications and conditions for harmless treatment.
Livestock and poultry farms are prohibited from using kitchen waste that has not undergone harmless treatment to feed livestock and poultry.

Article 515 Local people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the principle that the generator pays, establish and improve a fee system for domestic waste treatment.
When setting the fee standard for domestic waste treatment, local people's governments at or above the county level shall, based on local realities and the classification of domestic waste, reflect differentiated management such as classified pricing and metered charging, and fully solicit public opinions. The fee standard for domestic waste treatment shall be published in a timely manner.
The domestic waste treatment fee shall be used exclusively for the collection, transportation, and treatment of domestic waste, and shall not be diverted to other purposes.

Article 516 Local people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the prevention and control of construction waste pollution and establish a sound system for the classified treatment of construction waste.
For the purposes of this Law, "construction waste" means the waste soil, waste materials, and other solid waste generated during the construction, renovation, expansion, and demolition of various buildings, structures, and pipe networks by construction units and construction units, as well as during the decoration and renovation of houses by residents.

Article 517 Construction projects shall adopt building design plans, building materials and decoration materials, building components and equipment that are conducive to protecting the ecological environment, so as to reduce the generation of construction waste.
Building materials and decoration materials shall comply with national standards. It is prohibited to produce, sell, or use building materials and decoration materials whose toxic and hazardous substances exceed national standards.

Article 518 The environmental sanitation department of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the prevention and control of construction waste pollution, establish a sound whole-process management system for construction waste, implement manifest management in accordance with the provisions, regulate the generation, collection, storage, transportation, utilization, and disposal of construction waste, promote comprehensive utilization, strengthen the construction of facilities and sites for construction waste disposal, ensure disposal safety, and prevent environmental pollution. The specific measures for the management of construction waste shall be formulated by the competent department of housing and urban-rural development of the State Council.
No unit or individual may arbitrarily dump, pile, discard, scatter, spill, or burn construction waste.

Article 519 The construction unit shall, in accordance with the provisions, include the cost of construction waste pollution prevention and control in the project cost, and specify in the construction contract the liability of the construction unit for construction waste pollution prevention and control.

Article 520 The engineering construction unit shall prepare a construction waste treatment plan, take pollution prevention and control measures, and report it to the environmental sanitation department of the local people's government at or above the county level for archival filing.
The engineering construction unit shall promptly remove and transport solid waste such as construction waste generated during the construction process, and utilize or dispose of it in accordance with the provisions of the environmental sanitation department.

Article 521 The competent department of agriculture and rural affairs of the people's government at or above the county level shall be responsible for guiding the establishment of an agricultural solid waste recovery and utilization system, encouraging and guiding relevant entities and other producers and operators to collect, store, transport, utilize, and dispose of agricultural solid waste according to law, and strengthening supervision and management to prevent environmental pollution.
Agricultural solid waste as mentioned in this Law means solid waste generated in agricultural production activities.
Article 522 Entities and other producers and operators that generate agricultural solid waste shall adopt measures for recovery and utilization and other measures to prevent environmental pollution.

Article 523 The dismantling and disposal of products such as retired wind turbine blades, retired photovoltaic modules, and waste power batteries shall strengthen pollution prevention and control, and carry out refined and harmless dismantling and disposal in accordance with the provisions.
Article 524 It shall be prohibited to hand over end-of-life motor vehicles, vessels, etc. to enterprises or individuals that do not meet the prescribed conditions for recovery and dismantling.

Article 525 The competent department of urban drainage of the people's government at or above the county level shall incorporate sludge treatment and disposal facilities into the urban drainage and sewage treatment plan according to law, promote the simultaneous construction of sludge treatment and disposal facilities and sewage treatment facilities, encourage coordinated treatment and disposal, and the levy standard and compensation scope of sewage treatment fees shall cover the costs of sludge treatment and disposal and the normal operation costs of sewage treatment facilities.

Article 526 It shall be prohibited to dump, pile up, discard, scatter, spill, or burn sludge generated by urban sewage treatment facilities and sludge after treatment and disposal without authorization.
Entities engaged in water body dredging shall treat the sediment generated in the dredging process in accordance with state regulations to prevent environmental pollution.

Article 527 Laboratories at all levels and of all types and their sponsoring entities shall strengthen the management of solid waste generated by laboratories, and collect, store, transport, utilize, and dispose of laboratory solid waste according to law. Where laboratory solid waste is hazardous waste, it shall be managed as hazardous waste.

Article 528 Hazardous waste as mentioned in this Law means solid waste that is included in the national hazardous waste list or identified as having hazardous characteristics according to the hazardous waste identification standards and methods stipulated by the state.

Article 529 The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall, together with relevant departments, formulate the national hazardous waste list, and prescribe unified hazardous waste identification standards, methods, procedures, identification marks, and management requirements for identification units. The national hazardous waste list shall be dynamically adjusted.
The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall, based on the hazardous characteristics and generation quantities of hazardous waste, scientifically assess their environmental risks, implement graded and classified management, establish a sound whole-process information-based supervision system, and manage and share hazardous waste transfer data and information through information-based means.

Article 530 The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall organize relevant departments to compile construction plans for centralized hazardous waste disposal facilities and sites, scientifically assess hazardous waste disposal needs, rationally distribute centralized hazardous waste disposal facilities and sites, and ensure that hazardous waste within their respective administrative regions is properly disposed of.
When compiling construction plans for centralized hazardous waste disposal facilities and sites, opinions from relevant industry associations, enterprises and institutions, experts, and the public shall be solicited.
Adjacent provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may carry out regional cooperation to coordinate the construction of regional centralized hazardous waste disposal facilities and sites.

Article 531 Hazardous waste identification marks shall be placed on containers and packaging of hazardous waste, as well as on facilities and sites for collecting, storing, transporting, utilizing, and disposing of hazardous waste, in accordance with the provisions.

Article 532 An entity that generates hazardous waste shall formulate a hazardous waste management plan in accordance with state regulations; establish a hazardous waste management ledger, truthfully record relevant information, and declare to the competent department of ecological environment of the locality the types, quantities, flow directions, storage, utilization, disposal, and other relevant information of hazardous waste through the national hazardous waste information management system.
The hazardous waste management plan mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall include measures to reduce the quantity of hazardous waste generated and reduce the hazardous characteristics of hazardous waste, as well as measures for storage, utilization, and disposal of hazardous waste. The hazardous waste management plan shall be filed with the competent department of ecological environment of the locality where the entity generating hazardous waste is located.
Where an entity generating hazardous waste has obtained a pollutant discharge permit, it shall implement the provisions of the pollutant discharge permit management system.

Article 533 An entity that generates hazardous waste shall store, utilize, and dispose of hazardous waste in accordance with state regulations and the requirements of ecological and environmental protection standards.
No entity or individual may dump, pile up, discard, scatter, spill, or burn hazardous waste without authorization.

Article 534 An entity engaged in business activities of collecting, storing, utilizing, or disposing of hazardous waste shall obtain a license in accordance with state regulations. The specific management measures for licenses shall be formulated by the State Council.
It shall be prohibited to engage in business activities of collecting, storing, utilizing, or disposing of hazardous waste without a license or not in accordance with the requirements of the license.
It shall be prohibited to provide or entrust hazardous waste to an entity or individual without a license for engaging in collection, storage, utilization, or disposal activities.

Article 535 Collection and storage of hazardous waste shall be carried out by classification according to the characteristics of hazardous waste. It shall be prohibited to mix, collect, store, transport, or dispose of hazardous wastes that are incompatible in nature and have not undergone safety treatment.
Storage of hazardous waste shall adopt protective measures that conform to national ecological and environmental protection standards. It shall be prohibited to mix hazardous waste with non-hazardous waste for storage.
An entity engaged in business activities of collecting, storing, utilizing, or disposing of hazardous waste shall not store hazardous waste for more than one year; where extension of the period is truly necessary, approval shall be obtained from the competent department of ecological environment that issued the license, unless otherwise provided by laws or administrative regulations.

Article 536 Where hazardous waste is transferred, the electronic or paper-based transfer manifest for hazardous waste shall be filled in and operated in accordance with state regulations.
Where hazardous waste is transferred across provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government, an application shall be made to the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the hazardous waste is moved out. The competent department of ecological environment of the province where the waste is moved out shall, after promptly consulting with and obtaining consent from the competent department of ecological environment of the receiving province, approve the transfer of the hazardous waste within a specified period, and notify the relevant provincial competent departments of ecological environment and the competent department of transportation of the approval information. Without approval, no transfer shall be made.
The management of hazardous waste transfer shall ensure whole-process control and improve efficiency, and specific measures shall be formulated by the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council together with the competent department of transportation of the State Council and the public security department.

Article 537 When transporting hazardous waste, measures to prevent environmental pollution shall be taken, and the provisions of the state concerning the management of dangerous goods transport shall be complied with.
It shall be prohibited to carry hazardous waste together with passengers on the same means of transport.

Article 538 When places, facilities, equipment, containers, packaging, and other items used for collecting, storing, transporting, utilizing, or disposing of hazardous waste are converted to other uses, they shall undergo decontamination treatment in accordance with state regulations before they may be used.

Article 539 An entity that generates, collects, stores, transports, utilizes, or disposes of hazardous waste shall formulate preventive measures and emergency response plans for accidents according to law, and shall file them with the competent department of ecological environment of the locality and other departments responsible for supervision and management of solid waste pollution prevention and control; the competent department of ecological environment and other departments responsible for supervision and management of solid waste pollution prevention and control shall conduct supervision and inspection within their respective functions and duties.

Article 540 An entity that causes severe pollution from hazardous waste due to an accident or other emergency shall immediately take effective measures to eliminate or mitigate the pollution hazard, promptly notify those who may be harmed by the pollution, and report to the competent department of ecological environment of the locality and relevant departments, and accept investigation and handling.

Article 541 When a serious pollution or a threat to the life and property safety of residents caused by hazardous waste occurs or there is evidence proving that it may occur, the competent department of ecological environment and other departments responsible for the supervision and administration of the prevention and control of solid waste pollution shall immediately report to the people's government at the same level and the relevant departments of the people's government at the next higher level, and the people's government shall take effective measures to prevent or mitigate the harm. The relevant people's government may, based on actual needs, order the suspension of operations that cause or may cause environmental pollution accidents.

Article 542 Before the decommissioning of key centralized hazardous waste disposal facilities and sites, the operating units shall take pollution prevention and control measures for the facilities and sites in accordance with state regulations. The costs of decommissioning shall be accrued in advance, included in the investment estimate or production costs, and used exclusively for the decommissioning of key centralized hazardous waste disposal facilities and sites. The specific measures for accrual and management shall be formulated by the finance department and the price department of the State Council jointly with the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council.
Article 543 The transfer of hazardous waste through the territory of the People's Republic of China is prohibited.

Article 544 Medical waste shall be managed in accordance with the national list of hazardous wastes. Local people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the capacity building for centralized disposal of medical waste.
The health and ecological environment departments and other relevant departments shall, within their respective functions and duties, strengthen the supervision and management of the collection, storage, transportation, and disposal of medical waste, to prevent harm to public health and environmental pollution.
Medical and health institutions shall classify and collect the medical waste generated by their units according to law, and deliver it to the centralized medical waste disposal unit for disposal. The centralized medical waste disposal unit shall collect, transport, and dispose of medical waste in a timely manner.
Medical and health institutions and centralized medical waste disposal units shall take effective measures to prevent the loss, leakage, seepage, and spread of medical waste.

Article 545 When major infectious disease epidemics or other emergencies occur, the people's government at or above the county level shall coordinate the collection, storage, transportation, disposal, and other work of hazardous waste such as medical waste, and ensure the necessary vehicles, sites, disposal facilities, and protective materials. The health, ecological environment, environmental sanitation, transportation, and other relevant departments shall cooperate and perform emergency response duties according to law.
Division 7 Prevention and Control of Noise Pollution
Article 546 This Division applies to the prevention and control of noise pollution.

Article 547 For the purposes of this Law, "noise pollution" means a phenomenon in which noise exceeding the noise emission standards or generated without taking prevention and control measures according to law in industrial production, construction, transportation, and social life interferes with the normal life, work, and study of others.

Article 548 The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall exercise unified supervision and administration over the prevention and control of noise pollution nationwide. The competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government shall exercise unified supervision and administration over the prevention and control of noise pollution within its administrative region.
The relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level, such as housing and urban-rural construction, public security, transportation, railway supervision, civil aviation, and maritime affairs, shall, within their respective functions and duties, exercise supervision and administration over the prevention and control of noise pollution from construction, transportation, and social life.

Article 549 The grassroots self-governing mass organizations shall assist the local people's governments and their relevant departments in carrying out the work of prevention and control of noise pollution.

Article 550 Units that discharge noise and managers of public places shall establish a responsibility system for the prevention and control of noise pollution, and specify the responsibilities of the persons in charge and relevant personnel.

Article 551 When preparing territorial space plans and relevant plans, people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall fully consider the impact of noise generated by urban and rural regional development, renovation, and construction projects on the surrounding living environment, make overall plans, reasonably arrange land use and construction layout, and prevent and mitigate noise pollution.

Article 552 The people's governments of cities divided into districts and counties where areas fail to meet the national acoustic environment quality standards shall, in a timely manner, formulate plans for improving acoustic environment quality and implementation plans thereof, and take effective measures to improve the acoustic environment quality.

Article 553 The local people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the national acoustic environment quality standards, territorial space plans, and current land use, delimit the applicable areas for various types of acoustic environment quality standards within their administrative regions; and shall designate areas mainly consisting of buildings used for residence, scientific research, medical and health care, culture and education, government offices, social welfare, etc., as concentrated areas of noise-sensitive buildings, and strengthen the prevention and control of noise pollution.
The scope of applicable areas for acoustic environment quality standards and the scope of concentrated areas of noise-sensitive buildings shall be published in a timely manner.
For the purposes of this Law, "noise-sensitive buildings" means buildings used for residence, scientific research, medical and health care, culture and education, government offices, social welfare, etc., that require maintaining quietness.

Article 554 The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall, in accordance with the national acoustic environment quality standards and the national economic and technological conditions, formulate national environmental vibration control standards.
Vibrations generated shall comply with the environmental vibration control standards and the requirements of relevant laws, regulations, and rules.

Article 555 The competent department of standardization of the State Council shall, jointly with the relevant departments such as development and reform, ecological environment, industry and information technology, housing and urban-rural construction, transportation, railway supervision, civil aviation, and maritime affairs of the State Council, stipulate noise limits in the technical specifications or product quality standards for products that may cause noise pollution, such as industrial equipment, construction machinery, motor vehicles, railway rolling stock, urban rail transit vehicles, civil aircraft, motor vessels, electrical and electronic products, and building ancillary equipment, in accordance with the requirements of noise pollution prevention and control and the national economic and technological conditions.
The noise limits for the products specified in the preceding paragraph when in use shall be indicated in the relevant technical documents. The production, import, or sale of products that do not meet the noise limits is prohibited.
The market supervision and administration departments and other relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions and duties, conduct supervisory spot checks on products with noise limits that are produced and sold, and conduct supervisory sampling tests on noise emitted by special equipment such as elevators when in use, and the competent department of ecological environment shall cooperate.

Article 556 The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall, jointly with relevant departments, organize and carry out acoustic environment quality monitoring and promote the automation of monitoring. The competent department of ecological environment of local people's governments shall, jointly with relevant departments, set up acoustic environment quality monitoring stations in their administrative regions in accordance with regulations, and organize and carry out acoustic environment quality monitoring in their administrative regions.
The ecological environment and other relevant departments of local people's governments shall, within their respective functions and duties, strengthen the investigation and monitoring of noise emissions in key areas such as the vicinity of noise-sensitive buildings.

Article 557 When determining the construction layout, the noise prevention distance between buildings and traffic arteries, etc., shall be reasonably delimited in accordance with the national acoustic environment quality standards and relevant standards for sound insulation design of civil buildings, and corresponding planning and design requirements shall be put forward.
For the purposes of the preceding paragraph, "traffic arteries" include railways, expressways, Class I highways, Class II highways, urban expressways, urban trunk roads, urban secondary trunk roads, urban rail transit lines, and high-grade inland waterways.

Article 558 The construction of noise-sensitive buildings shall meet the requirements of relevant standards for sound insulation design of civil buildings; those that do not meet the standard requirements shall not pass acceptance inspection or be put into use. In addition, when constructing noise-sensitive buildings on both sides of traffic arteries, around industrial enterprises, or in other places, a certain distance shall be left in accordance with regulations, and measures to reduce vibration and noise shall be taken.
Article 559 The State encourages and supports the research, development, and promotion of low-noise processes and equipment.
Article 560 The State encourages the creation of quiet areas such as quiet residential communities and quiet train compartments, to jointly maintain a harmonious and peaceful living environment.

Article 561 During special activities such as secondary school entrance examinations and unified college entrance examinations, the local people's government or the department designated by it may impose restrictions on the time and area for activities that may produce noise impact, and shall announce such restrictions to the public in advance.

Article 562 If a person emits noise causing severe pollution and refuses to correct it after being ordered to do so, the competent department of ecological environment and other departments responsible for the supervision and administration of noise pollution prevention may, according to law, seal up or detain the premises, facilities, equipment, tools, and articles that emit noise.

Article 563 The prevention and control of noise hazards suffered from engaging in one's own production and operation work shall be governed by the relevant provisions of the occupational disease prevention and control law.
Article 564 Industrial noise as used in this Law means sounds generated during industrial production activities that interfere with the surrounding living environment.

Article 565 The site selection of industrial enterprises shall comply with the requirements of land and space planning and relevant planning. The local people's government at or above the county level shall optimize the layout of industrial enterprises in accordance with the planning requirements to prevent industrial noise pollution.

Article 566 In areas where noise-sensitive buildings are concentrated, it is prohibited to construct new industrial enterprises that emit noise. Those that reconstruct or expand industrial enterprises shall take effective measures to prevent industrial noise pollution.
Article 567 Enterprises, institutions, and other producers and business operators that emit industrial noise shall take effective measures to reduce vibration and lower noise.
Article 568 Construction noise as used in this Law means sounds generated during construction activities that interfere with the surrounding living environment.

Article 569 The construction unit shall, in accordance with the regulations, include the cost of noise pollution prevention and control in the project cost, and specify the noise pollution prevention and control responsibilities of the construction contractor in the construction contract.
The construction contractor shall, in accordance with the regulations, develop an implementation plan for noise pollution prevention and control, and take effective measures to reduce vibration and lower noise. The construction unit shall supervise the construction contractor in implementing the noise pollution prevention and control implementation plan.

Article 570 If construction operations are carried out in areas where noise-sensitive buildings are concentrated, or construction operations may cause severe pollution, low-noise construction techniques and equipment shall be used as a priority.
The competent department of industry and information technology of the State Council shall, together with the competent departments of ecological environment, housing and urban-rural construction, market supervision and administration, and other relevant departments of the State Council, formulate and publish a guidance list of low-noise construction equipment and update it in a timely manner.

Article 571 If construction operations are carried out in areas where noise-sensitive buildings are concentrated, or construction operations may cause severe pollution, the construction unit shall, in accordance with state regulations, set up an automatic noise monitoring system, connect it to the supervision and management department, and preserve original monitoring records.

Article 572 In areas where noise-sensitive buildings are concentrated, construction operations that generate noise are prohibited at night, except for emergency repair and rescue construction operations, or where construction operations must be continuous due to production process requirements or other special needs.
If continuous construction operations are necessary due to special needs, the construction unit shall obtain a certificate from the competent department of housing and urban-rural construction, the competent department of ecological environment, or the department designated by the local people's government, and shall post it at a conspicuous place at the construction site or otherwise notify nearby residents.
'Night' as used in the first paragraph of this Article means the period from 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. of the following day. The local people's government at or above the city divided into districts may separately prescribe the starting and ending times of night in its administrative area, provided that the duration of the night period is eight hours.

Article 573 Transportation noise as used in this Law means sounds generated during the operation of transportation vehicles such as motor vehicles, railway locomotives and carriages, urban rail transit vehicles, motor vessels, and aircraft that interfere with the surrounding living environment.

Article 574 When drawing up land and space planning and transportation and other relevant plans, the people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall comprehensively consider the impact of highways, urban roads, railways, urban rail transit lines, waterways, ports, and civil airports and their takeoff and landing routes on the surrounding acoustic environment.
The route selection and design of newly built highways and railway lines shall, to the extent possible, avoid areas where noise-sensitive buildings are concentrated.
The distance between the site selection of a newly built civil airport and the areas where noise-sensitive buildings are concentrated shall comply with the requirements of the standards.

Article 575 When formulating engineering technical specifications for transportation infrastructure, the requirements for noise pollution prevention and control shall be specified.
If newly built, reconstructed, or expanded highways, urban viaducts, railway lines, and urban rail transit lines pass through areas where noise-sensitive buildings are concentrated, the construction unit shall install sound barriers on key sections that may cause noise pollution or take other measures to reduce vibration and lower noise, and shall comply with the requirements of relevant engineering technical specifications and standards for transportation infrastructure.
If the construction unit violates the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the department designated by the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to formulate and implement a remediation plan.

Article 576 The mufflers and horns of motor vehicles shall comply with state regulations. It is prohibited to drive a motor vehicle that has been modified without authorization, such as by removing or damaging the muffler or adding an exhaust pipe, to cause noise pollution by roaring or speeding.
When using audio equipment on a motor vehicle, the volume shall be controlled to prevent noise pollution.
Motor vehicles shall undergo strengthened repair and maintenance to maintain good performance and prevent noise pollution.

Article 577 When motor vehicles, railway locomotives and carriages, urban rail transit vehicles, motor vessels, and other transportation vehicles are in operation, they shall use horns and other sound devices in accordance with regulations.
The installation and use of sirens on motor vehicles such as police cars, fire engines, emergency rescue vehicles, and ambulances shall comply with the provisions of the public security department of the State Council and other relevant departments; they shall not use sirens when not on emergency duties.

Article 578 The competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government together with the public security organ may, based on the needs of noise pollution prevention and control, designate sections of road and time periods where motor vehicle driving and use of horns and other sound devices are prohibited, announce such designations to the public, and the traffic management department of the public security organ shall set up relevant signs and markings according to law.
Article 579 When using loudspeakers to direct operations at stations, railway yards, ports, and other places, the volume shall be controlled to reduce noise pollution.

Article 580 The highway maintenance and management unit and the urban road maintenance and repair unit shall strengthen the maintenance and upkeep of highways and urban roads to ensure the normal operation of facilities for reducing vibration and lowering noise.
The urban rail transit operation unit and the railway transport enterprise shall strengthen the maintenance and upkeep of urban rail transit lines and urban rail transit vehicles, railway lines and railway locomotives and carriages, to ensure the normal operation of facilities for reducing vibration and lowering noise, and shall conduct monitoring in accordance with state regulations and preserve original monitoring records.
