Article 581 The people's government of the place where a civil airport is located shall, based on the scope and degree of impact of civil aircraft noise on the living environment around the airport as determined by the ecological environment impact assessment and monitoring results, delineate areas where construction of noise-sensitive buildings is prohibited and areas where such construction is restricted, and shall implement controls.
Construction of noise-sensitive buildings unrelated to aviation is prohibited in the prohibited area.
Where it is truly necessary to construct noise-sensitive buildings in the restricted area, the construction entity shall carry out architectural sound insulation design for the noise-sensitive buildings, meeting the requirements of relevant standards for sound insulation design of civil buildings.
Article 582 Civil aircraft shall comply with the noise requirements in the airworthiness standards prescribed by the civil aviation authority under the State Council.

Article 583 The civil airport management authority shall be responsible for the management of noise from aircraft taking off and landing at the airport, and shall, together with air transport enterprises, general aviation enterprises, air traffic control departments and other entities, adopt measures such as low-noise flight procedures, optimization of take-off and landing runways, control of flight sorties and time periods, restrictions on operation of high-noise aircraft, or sound insulation and noise reduction for surrounding noise-sensitive buildings, to prevent and mitigate civil aircraft noise pollution.
The civil airport management authority shall, in accordance with state regulations, monitor civil aircraft noise around the airport, retain original monitoring records, and regularly report the monitoring results to the civil aviation authority and the ecological environment authority.

Article 584 Where serious pollution is caused by noise emitted from the operation of highways, urban roads and urban rail transit, the people's government of a city with districts or at the county level shall organize relevant departments and other relevant entities to investigate and assess the noise pollution situation and determine liability, and shall formulate a comprehensive noise pollution control plan.
The subject liable for noise pollution shall take management or engineering measures in accordance with the requirements of the comprehensive noise pollution control plan to mitigate the noise pollution.

Article 585 Where serious pollution is caused by noise emitted from railway operations, the railway transport enterprise and the people's government of a city with districts or at the county level shall investigate the noise pollution situation and formulate a comprehensive noise pollution control plan.
The railway transport enterprise and the relevant departments of the people's government of a city with districts or at the county level, as well as other relevant entities, shall take effective measures in accordance with the requirements of the comprehensive noise pollution control plan to mitigate the noise pollution.

Article 586 Where serious pollution is caused by noise emitted from the take-off and landing of civil aircraft, the people's government of the place where the civil airport is located shall organize relevant departments and other relevant entities to investigate the noise pollution situation, comprehensively consider economic, technical and management measures, and formulate a comprehensive noise pollution control plan.
The civil airport management authority, local people's governments at all levels and other relevant entities shall take effective measures in accordance with the requirements of the comprehensive noise pollution control plan to mitigate the noise pollution.
Article 587 When formulating a comprehensive noise pollution control plan, opinions of relevant experts, the public and other parties shall be solicited.

Article 588 For the purposes of this Law, social life noise means sounds generated by human activities, other than industrial noise, construction noise and traffic noise, that interfere with the surrounding living environment.

Article 589 The whole society shall enhance awareness of noise pollution prevention and control, consciously reduce social life noise emissions, actively carry out noise pollution prevention and control activities, create a good atmosphere of noise pollution prevention and control in which everyone has responsibility, everyone participates, and everyone benefits, and jointly maintain a harmonious and tranquil living environment.
Article 590 The operators and managers of venues such as cultural entertainment, sports, and catering shall take effective measures to prevent and mitigate noise pollution.

Article 591 Enterprises, institutions, and other operators and managers that use equipment and facilities such as air conditioners, cooling towers, water pumps, fume purifiers, fans, generators, transformers, boilers, loading and unloading equipment, which may generate social life noise pollution, shall take measures such as optimizing layout and centralized discharge to prevent and mitigate noise pollution.

Article 592 The use of high-pitched loudspeakers or other methods of continuously and repeatedly emitting high noise for advertising in commercial business activities is prohibited.
For other noise generated in commercial business activities, the operator shall take effective measures to prevent noise pollution.

Article 593 The use of high-pitched loudspeakers in areas concentrated with noise-sensitive buildings is prohibited, except in emergency situations and special circumstances as prescribed by the local people's government.
When organizing or carrying out entertainment, fitness, or other activities in public places such as streets, squares, and parks, the provisions of the public place manager regarding activity areas, time periods, and volume shall be complied with, and effective measures shall be taken to prevent noise pollution; sound equipment shall not be used in violation of regulations to produce excessive volume.
The manager of a public place shall reasonably stipulate the areas, time periods, and volume for entertainment, fitness, and other activities, and may take measures such as installing noise automatic monitoring and display facilities to strengthen management.

Article 594 Families and their members shall cultivate good habits of reducing noise generation, and in activities such as using public transportation, keeping pets, and other daily activities, shall try to avoid generating noise that causes disturbance to surrounding persons, resolve noise disputes through mutual understanding and accommodation, and jointly maintain the quality of the acoustic environment.
When using household appliances, musical instruments, or engaging in other activities in family premises, the volume shall be controlled or other effective measures shall be taken to prevent noise pollution.

Article 595 When carrying out interior decoration activities on buildings such as residential buildings, shops, and office buildings that have been completed and delivered for use, the operation time shall be limited in accordance with regulations, and effective measures shall be taken to prevent and mitigate noise pollution.

Article 596 The real estate development operator of newly-built residential housing shall, at the sales site, disclose the circumstances under which the housing may be affected by noise and the prevention and control measures taken or to be taken, and shall incorporate these into the sales contract.
The real estate development operator of newly-built residential housing shall specify in the sales contract the locations of common facilities and equipment of the housing and the building sound insulation conditions.

Article 597 Where common facilities and equipment such as elevators, water pumps, and transformers are installed in a residential area, the construction entity shall install them reasonably, take measures to reduce vibration and lower noise, and meet the requirements of relevant standards for sound insulation design of civil buildings.
The common facilities and equipment such as elevators, water pumps, and transformers in a residential area that has been completed and put into use shall be maintained and managed by a professional operating entity, and shall meet the requirements of relevant standards for sound insulation design of civil buildings.

Article 598 A grassroots self-governing mass organization shall guide the owners' committee, property service provider, and owners to stipulate the requirements for noise pollution prevention and control in the property management area through the formulation of management covenants or other forms, to be jointly observed by the owners.

Article 599 In the event of social life noise nuisance in areas concentrated with noise-sensitive buildings, the grassroots self-governing mass organization, owners' committee, and property service provider shall promptly dissuade and mediate; if dissuasion and mediation are ineffective, they may report or complain to the department responsible for supervision and administration of social life noise pollution prevention and control or the department designated by the local people's government, and the department receiving the report or complaint shall handle it according to law.
Division 8 Prevention and Control of Radioactive Pollution

Article 600 This Division applies to the prevention and control of radioactive pollution occurring in the processes of siting, construction, operation, and decommissioning of nuclear facilities, and the development and utilization of nuclear technology, uranium (thorium) mines, and associated radioactive mines.

For the purposes of this Law, "radioactive pollution" means the presence of radioactive substances or radiation exceeding national standards in materials, human bodies, places, environmental media surfaces or interiors due to human activities.
The prevention and control of radioactive pollution shall adhere to strict management, safety first, and promote the development and peaceful use of nuclear energy and nuclear technology.

Nuclear facility operating entities, nuclear technology utilization entities and other producers and operators, uranium (thorium) mines and associated radioactive mine development and utilization entities, and entities specialized in the storage, treatment and disposal of radioactive waste shall take effective measures to prevent and reduce radioactive pollution, and bear liability for radioactive pollution caused by them according to law.
Production, storage, transportation, sale, use and disposal of articles containing radioactive substances shall comply with state regulations to prevent environmental pollution.

The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall implement unified supervision and administration over the national prevention and control of radioactive pollution.
The competent departments of health and other relevant departments under the State Council shall implement supervision and administration over the prevention and control of radioactive pollution within their respective responsibilities.

The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall formulate national standards for the prevention and control of radioactive pollution in accordance with environmental safety requirements and national economic and technological conditions.

Products containing radioactive substances and radiation devices shall conform to national standards for the prevention and control of radioactive pollution; those that do not conform to national standards for the prevention and control of radioactive pollution shall not be delivered from factory or sold.
Use of associated radioactive mine slag and stone materials containing natural radioactive substances shall conform to national standards for control of radionuclides in building materials, etc.

The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall, together with relevant departments, organize a monitoring network to implement monitoring and management of radioactive pollution.

Nuclear facility operating entities, nuclear technology utilization entities and other producers and operators, uranium (thorium) mines and associated radioactive mine development and utilization entities, and entities specialized in the storage, treatment and disposal of radioactive waste shall take safety and protection measures to prevent various accidents that may cause radioactive pollution and avoid radioactive pollution hazards.
Nuclear facility operating entities, nuclear technology utilization entities and other producers and operators, uranium (thorium) mines and associated radioactive mine development and utilization entities, and entities specialized in the storage, treatment and disposal of radioactive waste shall provide radioactive safety education and training to their staff and take effective protection safety measures.
Transportation of radioactive substances shall take effective measures to prevent radioactive pollution. Specific measures shall be formulated by the State Council.

Radioactive substances and radiation devices shall be provided with clear radioactive identification and Chinese warning instructions. Places where radioactive substances and radiation devices are produced, stored, sold, used or disposed of, and tools for transporting radioactive substances, shall be provided with clear radioactive signs.

The competent departments of ecological environment and other relevant departments under the State Council shall exchange information and cooperate closely, and shall supervise and inspect the prevention and control of radioactive pollution in nuclear facilities, nuclear technology utilization, and development and utilization of uranium (thorium) mines within their respective responsibilities.
The competent departments of ecological environment and other relevant departments of local people's governments shall exchange information and cooperate closely, and shall supervise and inspect the prevention and control of radioactive pollution in nuclear technology utilization and development and utilization of associated radioactive mines within their respective responsibilities in their administrative regions.

The State shall establish a radioactive pollution prevention and control system that conforms to the characteristics of controlled thermonuclear fusion and promotes the application of nuclear fusion, and implement graded and classified management for the prevention and control of radioactive pollution from fusion fuels and fusion devices (facilities). The construction of fusion devices (facilities) shall undergo ecological environment impact assessment according to law.

The prevention and treatment of occupational diseases caused by exposure to radioactive substances in occupational activities shall be governed by the relevant provisions of the Law on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases.

Nuclear facility operating entities engaging in activities such as siting, construction, operation, and decommissioning of nuclear facilities shall apply for nuclear facility safety licenses according to law.
For the purposes of this Law, "nuclear facilities" means nuclear power plants, nuclear heating plants, nuclear steam and heat supply plants and other nuclear power installations and devices, other reactors such as research reactors, experimental reactors, and critical assemblies other than nuclear power installations, nuclear fuel cycle facilities such as nuclear fuel production, processing, storage and reprocessing facilities, and facilities for the storage, treatment and disposal of radioactive waste generated by the above facilities.

Nuclear facility operating entities shall carry out ecological environment impact assessments in the construction, decommissioning, siting, and operation stages of nuclear facilities in accordance with the provisions of the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council.

The import of nuclear facilities shall conform to national standards for the prevention and control of radioactive pollution; where there are no corresponding national standards for the prevention and control of radioactive pollution, the relevant standards designated by the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall be adopted.

The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, according to law, delineate planned restricted zones around important nuclear facilities such as nuclear power plants. Construction of facilities for the production and storage of flammable, explosive, or corrosive articles that may threaten the safety of nuclear facilities, and densely populated places, shall be prohibited within the planned restricted zones. The measures for the delineation and administration of planned restricted zones shall be formulated by the State Council.

Nuclear facility operating entities shall monitor the types and concentrations of radionuclides contained in the surrounding environment of nuclear facilities and the total amount of radionuclides in the effluents of nuclear facilities, and shall regularly report the monitoring results to the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council and the competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government where the facility is located.
The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall be responsible for implementing supervised monitoring of important nuclear facilities such as nuclear power plants, and shall monitor the effluents of other nuclear facilities as necessary. The costs of construction, operation and maintenance of the supervised monitoring system shall be arranged by the financial budget.

The State shall establish and improve the nuclear accident emergency response system.
The State shall establish a nuclear accident emergency coordination committee to organize and coordinate the national nuclear accident emergency management work. The member units of the National Nuclear Accident Emergency Coordination Committee, the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and nuclear facility operating entities shall well perform the nuclear accident emergency work according to law.

Article 621 The operator of a nuclear facility shall formulate a decommissioning plan for the nuclear facility.
The decommissioning costs of the nuclear facility and the disposal costs of radioactive waste shall be pre-appropriated, included in the investment estimate or production cost, and used exclusively for the decommissioning of the nuclear facility and the disposal of radioactive waste. The measures for the appropriation and management of the decommissioning costs of the nuclear facility and the disposal costs of radioactive waste shall be formulated by the financial department and the price administration department of the State Council jointly with the competent department of ecological environment, the competent department of nuclear industry, and the competent department of energy of the State Council.

Article 622 The State shall strengthen the prevention and control of radioactive pollution from the use of nuclear technology. The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall implement graded and classified management of radioactive isotopes and radiation devices that may cause pollution.
For the purposes of this Law, “use of nuclear technology” means the use of radioactive isotopes and radiation devices in such fields as medical treatment, industry, agriculture, geological survey, scientific research, and teaching.

Article 623 Units and other producers and business operators that produce, sell, or use radioactive isotopes and radiation devices shall obtain licenses in accordance with the provisions of the State Council on radiation protection of radioactive isotopes and radiation devices. Without obtaining a license, no one may engage in the production, sale, or use of radioactive isotopes and radiation devices. It is prohibited to sell radioactive isotopes and radiation devices on the Internet.
Units and other producers and business operators that transfer, import, or export radioactive isotopes and radiation devices, and units and other producers and business operators that are equipped with instruments containing radioactive isotopes, shall handle relevant procedures in accordance with the provisions of the State Council on radiation protection of radioactive isotopes and radiation devices.

Article 624 Units and other producers and business operators that produce, sell, or use radioactive isotopes and radiation devices shall, before applying for a license, obtain approval documents for the ecological environment impact report or the ecological environment impact form, or have completed the filing procedures for the ecological environment impact registration form in accordance with law.
The State shall establish and improve a filing system for radioactive isotopes, and the specific measures shall be formulated by the State Council.

Article 625 Radioactive isotopes shall be stored separately and shall not be stored together with flammable, explosive, corrosive, or other articles. Effective fire-proof, theft-proof, and radiation leakage-proof safety protection measures shall be taken for their storage premises, and special personnel shall be designated to be responsible for custody. When storing, collecting, using, or returning radioactive isotopes, registration and inspection shall be carried out to ensure that the accounts and physical objects are consistent.

Article 626 Units and other producers and business operators that produce or use radioactive isotopes and radiation devices shall collect, package, and store the radioactive waste generated by them in accordance with the provisions of the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council.
Units and other producers and business operators that produce radioactive sources shall recover and utilize spent radioactive sources in accordance with the provisions of the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council; units and other producers and business operators that use radioactive sources shall return spent radioactive sources to the units and other producers and business operators that produce radioactive sources, or deliver them to units specialized in the storage, treatment, or disposal of radioactive waste, in accordance with the provisions of the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council.

Article 627 Sites using radioactive sources with a higher degree of potential harm to human health and the ecological environment, sites producing radioactive isotopes, and radiation devices that generate radioactive pollution after termination of operation shall be decommissioned in accordance with law. The specific measures shall be formulated by the State Council.

Article 628 Units and other producers and business operators that produce, store, sell, or use radioactive sources shall establish and improve a security system, designate special personnel to be responsible, implement a safety responsibility system, and formulate necessary accident emergency measures. When a radioactive source is lost or stolen or a radioactive pollution accident occurs, the relevant unit or individual shall immediately take emergency measures and report to the public security organ, the competent department of health, and the competent department of ecological environment.
After receiving a report on the loss or theft of a radioactive source or a radioactive pollution accident, the public security organ, the competent department of health, and the competent department of ecological environment shall report to the people's government at the same level, and immediately organize the adoption of effective measures within their respective functions and duties to prevent the spread of radioactive pollution and reduce accident losses. The local people's government shall promptly inform the public of the relevant situation and handle the investigation and treatment of the accident properly.

Article 629 Units that exploit, develop, or close uranium (thorium) mines shall, before commencing construction or handling decommissioning approval procedures, prepare an ecological environment impact report or an ecological environment impact form, and submit it to the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council for review and approval.
Units that exploit and develop associated radioactive mines shall, before commencing construction or decommissioning, prepare an ecological environment impact report or an ecological environment impact form, and submit it to the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the provincial level for review and approval.
For the purposes of this Law, “associated radioactive mines” means non-uranium mines such as rare earth mines and phosphate mines that contain a relatively high concentration of natural radionuclides and are included in the list for radiation environment management of the exploitation and development of associated radioactive mines.

Article 630 The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall, based on the degree of potential harm of radionuclides in the exploitation and utilization of mineral resources to human health and the ecological environment, formulate a list for radiation environment management of the exploitation and development of associated radioactive mines, which shall uniformly stipulate the judgment methods and standards, mineral categories, and industrial activities to be included in the radiation environment management of the exploitation and development of associated radioactive mines. The list for radiation environment management of the exploitation and development of associated radioactive mines shall be subject to dynamic adjustment.

Article 631 For units exploiting and developing associated radioactive mines that are subject to pollutant discharge permit management, the pollutant discharge permit shall record information such as the types, concentrations, and discharge amounts of radionuclides in discharged waste liquids, the categories, physical properties, generation links, and destinations of associated radioactive solid waste, and the self-storage, utilization, and disposal of associated radioactive solid waste and related facilities.

Article 632 Units that exploit and develop uranium (thorium) mines shall monitor the effluents from the uranium (thorium) mines and the surrounding environment, and regularly report the monitoring results to the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council and the competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government where the mine is located.

Article 333 Radioactive solid waste such as tailings generated in the process of exploitation and development of uranium (thorium) mines and associated radioactive mines shall be stored and disposed of by constructing tailings ponds and other facilities; the constructed tailings ponds and other facilities shall meet the requirements for the prevention and control of radioactive pollution.

Article 634 Units that exploit and develop uranium (thorium) mines shall formulate a decommissioning plan for the uranium (thorium) mine. The costs of decommissioning and monitoring of uranium mines shall be arranged from the state financial budget.

Article 635 Operators of nuclear facilities, units using nuclear technology, and other producers and business operators, and units exploiting and developing uranium (thorium) mines and associated radioactive mines shall rationally select and utilize raw materials, adopt advanced production processes and equipment, and minimize the generation of radioactive waste.
Radioactive waste means waste that contains radionuclides or is contaminated by radionuclides and whose concentration or specific activity is greater than the clearance level determined by the State and that is no longer expected to be used. The specific measures for clearance shall be formulated by the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council.
Article 636 The discharge of radioactive waste gas and waste liquid shall comply with the provisions and standards of the State on the prevention and control of radioactive pollution.

Article 637 Units that generate radioactive waste gas and waste liquid and discharge radioactive waste gas and waste liquid that comply with the provisions and standards of the State on the prevention and control of radioactive pollution shall apply to the competent department of ecological environment that approved the ecological environment impact report or ecological environment impact form for the discharge amount of radionuclides, and regularly report the discharge measurement results.

Article 638 Units that generate radioactive waste liquid shall, in accordance with the requirements of the provisions and standards of the State on the prevention and control of radioactive pollution, treat or store radioactive waste liquid that may not be discharged. Radioactive waste liquid that cannot meet the provisions and standards of the State on the prevention and control of radioactive pollution after purification or storage decay shall be converted into stable, standardized radioactive solid waste that meets the disposal requirements.
Units that generate radioactive waste liquid and discharge radioactive waste liquid that complies with the provisions and standards of the State on the prevention and control of radioactive pollution shall adopt a discharge method that conforms to the provisions of the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council.
It is prohibited to discharge radioactive waste liquid through seepage wells, seepage pits, natural fissures, karst caves, or other means prohibited by the State.

Article 639 Low- and intermediate-level radioactive solid waste shall undergo near-surface disposal or intermediate-depth disposal in accordance with State regulations.
High-level radioactive solid waste shall undergo centralized deep geological disposal.
It is prohibited to dispose of radioactive solid waste in inland waters and at sea.

Article 640 The competent department of nuclear industry of the State Council shall, jointly with the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council, based on geological conditions and the needs for the disposal of radioactive solid waste, and on the basis of ecological environment impact assessment, organize the formulation of a siting plan for radioactive solid waste disposal sites in accordance with law, and submit it to the State Council for approval before implementation.
The relevant local people's government shall, in accordance with the siting plan for radioactive solid waste disposal sites, provide construction land for radioactive solid waste disposal sites and take effective measures to support the disposal of radioactive solid waste.

Article 641 A unit that generates radioactive solid waste shall, in accordance with the provisions of the competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council, treat the radioactive solid waste generated by it and then deliver it to a radioactive waste disposal unit for disposal, and shall bear the disposal costs.
The measures for the collection and use of radioactive solid waste disposal fees shall be formulated by the finance department and the price department of the State Council jointly with the competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council.

Article 642 An entity engaged exclusively in the storage, treatment, or disposal of radioactive waste shall be subject to the review and approval of the competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council and shall obtain a license; an entity that only stores or treats radioactive waste generated by itself need not obtain a license. The specific measures shall be formulated by the State Council.
It is prohibited to engage exclusively in the activities of storage, treatment, or disposal of radioactive waste without a license or not in accordance with the requirements of the license.
It is prohibited to provide or entrust radioactive waste to any unit or individual without a license for storage, treatment, or disposal.

Article 643 It is prohibited to import radioactive waste or articles contaminated by radioactivity into the territory of the People's Republic of China, or to transfer them through the territory of the People's Republic of China, in violation of the provisions of laws.
Division 9 Risk Control of Chemical Substance Pollution, Prevention and Control of Electromagnetic Radiation and Light Pollution

Article 644 The State shall strengthen risk control of chemical substance pollution. The production, import, storage, transportation, sale, use, and disposal of chemical substances shall comply with the provisions of the State to prevent environmental pollution and protect public health. The specific measures shall be formulated by the State Council.

Article 645 The State shall establish a coordinated governance and environmental risk control system for new pollutants such as persistent organic pollutants. The competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council shall, jointly with relevant departments, analyze and assess the situation of environmental risk control of new pollutants, formulate and improve relevant standards, organize and conduct investigation and monitoring, and effectively reduce the environmental risks of new pollutants.

Article 646 The competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council shall exercise unified supervision and administration over the work of risk control of chemical substance pollution nationwide. The relevant departments of the State Council, including those for development and reform, industry and information technology, agriculture and rural affairs, commerce, health, customs, market regulation, disease prevention and control, and drug administration, shall exercise supervision and administration over the work of risk control of chemical substance pollution within their respective functions and duties.
Local people's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall strengthen risk control of chemical substance pollution.

Article 647 The competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council shall, on the basis of the hazardous characteristics of chemical substances, organize periodic investigations into chemical substance pollution information. Enterprises and institutions that produce, import, sell chemical substances or use chemical substances to produce products shall, in accordance with the provisions, provide information such as the physical and chemical properties, quantity, use, hazardous characteristics, and emissions of the chemical substances required for the investigation.

Article 648 The relevant departments of the State Council shall, within their respective functions and duties and in accordance with the provisions, take effective measures to promote the substitution of toxic and hazardous chemical substances.

Article 649 The competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council shall, jointly with relevant departments, organize and conduct risk assessment of chemical substance pollution, formulate and publish a list of new pollutants subject to priority control and adjust it in a timely manner, and specify environmental risk control measures such as prohibition and restriction. Any entity that produces or imports a chemical substance on the list of new pollutants subject to priority control, or uses such a chemical substance to produce a product, shall comply with the aforementioned environmental risk control measures.

Article 650 The State shall implement a registration system for environmental management of new chemical substances.
An enterprise or institution that produces or imports a new chemical substance shall, before production or import, apply to the competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council for the registration of environmental management of the new chemical substance.

Article 651 It is prohibited to produce or import a new chemical substance without a registration certificate for environmental management of new chemical substances, or not in accordance with the requirements of the registration certificate. It is prohibited to use a new chemical substance produced or imported by an enterprise or institution without a registration certificate for environmental management of new chemical substances to produce products.
Article 652 Where this Chapter does not provide for the prevention and control of chemical substance pollution, the relevant provisions of this Division shall apply.

Article 653 For the purposes of this Law, electromagnetic radiation pollution means non-ionizing radiation generated by human activities that exceeds the national standards for electromagnetic radiation emission.

Article 654 The competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council shall exercise unified supervision and administration over the prevention and control of electromagnetic radiation pollution nationwide. The competent department of ecology and environment of a local people's government shall exercise unified supervision and administration over the prevention and control of electromagnetic radiation pollution in its administrative region.
The relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level, including those for industry and information technology, transportation, health, radio and television, meteorology, and energy, shall exercise supervision and administration over the prevention and control of electromagnetic radiation pollution within their respective functions and duties.

Article 655 When formulating territorial spatial plans and relevant plans, the people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall give full consideration to the impact of electromagnetic radiation generated by electromagnetic radiation facilities on the surrounding environment, make overall plans, reasonably arrange land use and construction layout, and prevent or mitigate electromagnetic radiation pollution.
The competent department of ecology and environment shall strengthen investigation and monitoring of electromagnetic radiation emissions.

Article 656 A local people's government at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the national electromagnetic environment quality standards, territorial spatial planning, and current land use conditions, delimit the applicable areas of various electromagnetic environment quality standards in its administrative region. The scope of applicable areas of electromagnetic environment quality standards shall be published in a timely manner.

Article 657 The competent department of standardization of the State Council shall, jointly with the relevant departments of the State Council, including those for ecology and environment, industry and information technology, transportation, railway supervision, civil aviation, maritime affairs, radio and television, meteorology, energy, and drug administration, prescribe electromagnetic radiation limits in the technical specifications or product quality standards for products that may cause electromagnetic radiation pollution, such as industrial equipment, radio transmitting equipment, telecommunication equipment, motor vehicles, railway locomotives and rolling stock, urban rail transit vehicles, navigation equipment, motor vessels, meteorological equipment, electrical and electronic equipment, and medical equipment, in accordance with the requirements for the prevention and control of electromagnetic radiation pollution and the national economic and technical conditions.
The limits on electromagnetic radiation generated during the use of the products specified in the preceding paragraph shall be indicated in the relevant technical documents. It is prohibited to produce, import, or sell any product that does not meet the electromagnetic radiation limits.
The relevant departments, such as the market regulation department, of the people's government at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions and duties, conduct supervisory random inspections on products with electromagnetic radiation limits that are produced and sold.

Article 658 The State shall implement categorized management of electromagnetic radiation facilities, and classify electromagnetic radiation facilities into Category I, Category II, and Category III based on the level of electromagnetic radiation emission and their impact on the surrounding environment. The specific measures shall be formulated by the competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council jointly with relevant departments.

Article 659 An enterprise or institution operating an electromagnetic radiation facility shall optimize the layout, reasonably arrange the electromagnetic radiation facilities, and take effective measures to prevent or mitigate electromagnetic radiation pollution.
An enterprise or institution operating an electromagnetic radiation facility shall, in accordance with the provisions of the State, build supporting facilities for the prevention and control of electromagnetic radiation pollution, and ensure the normal operation of such pollution prevention and control facilities.

Article 660 An enterprise or institution operating a Category I or Category II electromagnetic radiation facility shall, in accordance with the provisions of the State, take electromagnetic radiation pollution prevention and control measures such as transmission power control, transmission direction adjustment, emergency shutdown, shielding, grounding, and isolation, conduct self-monitoring, retain original monitoring records, and report the monitoring results to the competent department of ecology and environment on a regular basis.

Article 661 Enterprises and institutions operating Category I electromagnetic radiation facilities shall, in accordance with national regulations, set up warning signs and take measures such as installing fences to prevent close contact by the public and other electromagnetic radiation pollution prevention and control measures. New construction, renovation, and expansion of Category I electromagnetic radiation facilities shall avoid densely populated areas.

Article 662 The pollutant discharge permit of enterprises and institutions operating electromagnetic radiation facilities that are subject to pollutant discharge permit management shall record information such as the operating frequency, transmission power, field strength of the electromagnetic radiation facilities, and the situation of cumulative electromagnetic radiation effects.

Article 663 The use of mobile information transmission facilities shall, in accordance with national regulations, scientifically and reasonably demarcate protection distances, and take protective measures such as setting up warning lines and warning signs.

Article 664 The responsible entity for a device shared by multiple electromagnetic radiation facilities shall reasonably determine the number, location, power, etc. of the electromagnetic radiation facilities, and take effective measures to prevent electromagnetic radiation pollution caused by cumulative electromagnetic radiation effects.

Article 665 Where electromagnetic radiation facilities involving national security or major public interests cause serious electromagnetic radiation pollution, the local people's government at or above the county level shall organize relevant departments and other relevant units to investigate, assess, and determine liability for the electromagnetic radiation pollution, and comprehensively consider economic, technical, and management measures to formulate a comprehensive electromagnetic radiation pollution treatment plan.
The responsible party for electromagnetic radiation pollution shall take effective measures in accordance with the requirements of the comprehensive electromagnetic radiation pollution treatment plan to mitigate electromagnetic radiation pollution.

Article 666 The prevention and treatment of occupational diseases caused by exposure to electromagnetic radiation in occupational activities shall be governed by the relevant provisions of the law on the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases.

Article 667 For the purposes of this Law, "light pollution" means the phenomenon of excessive or improper use of artificial lighting or improper alteration of sunlight conditions, resulting in disturbance to the human vision in the surrounding living environment.

Article 668 The competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council shall exercise unified supervision and administration over the prevention and control of light pollution nationwide. The competent departments of ecology and environment of local people's governments shall exercise unified supervision and administration over the prevention and control of light pollution within their respective administrative regions.
Relevant departments such as housing and urban-rural development, transportation, etc. of the people's governments at or above the county level shall exercise supervision and administration over the prevention and control of light pollution within the scope of their respective duties.

Article 669 When formulating territorial space plans and related plans, people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall fully consider the potential light pollution impacts of urban and rural area development, renovation, and construction projects, carry out overall planning, and rationally arrange land use and construction layouts to prevent and mitigate light pollution.

Article 670 The competent department of standardization of the State Council shall, together with relevant departments such as housing and urban-rural development, ecology and environment, transportation, etc. of the State Council, in light of the requirements for light pollution prevention and control and the national economic and technical conditions, prescribe reasonable light limit values in their technical specifications or product quality standards for lighting products, outdoor display products, traffic fill lights, architectural glass and materials, etc.

Article 671 Advertising screens, billboards, light boxes, media façade walls, roads, stadiums, construction sites, etc. shall, in accordance with national regulations, reasonably design, install, and use lighting facilities, perform regular maintenance, and take effective measures to prevent and mitigate light pollution.

Article 672 The use of building materials such as glass curtain walls on the exterior surfaces of buildings and structures shall comply with national regulations, and the design and material selection shall be rational to prevent and mitigate light pollution.

Article 673 Local people's governments at or above the county level shall, based on actual circumstances, implement zoning management for light pollution prevention and control, and strengthen control over artificial lighting and sunlight conditions in areas requiring special protection.
Article 674 This Part applies to activities related to ecological protection.

Article 675 The state shall take into comprehensive consideration the complexity of ecological and environmental factors, the integrity of ecosystems, the continuity of natural geographical units, and the sustainability of economic and social development, adhere to the integrated protection and systematic governance of mountains, waters, forests, farmlands, grasslands, deserts, and glaciers, enhance the diversity, stability, and sustainability of ecosystems, and maintain ecological security.

Article 676 The state shall, based on the positioning of main functional zones, optimize the layout of ecological spaces, promote the protection and construction of national key ecological function zones and important ecological corridors, and build a solid ecological security barrier.

Article 677 The state shall strengthen the protection of ecosystems such as forests, grasslands, wetlands, oceans, islands, rivers and lakes, deserts, snowy mountains and glaciers, and farmlands, adhere to the principle of giving priority to natural recovery and combining natural recovery with artificial restoration, promote and implement major projects for the protection and restoration of important ecosystems, cultivate healthy, stable, and fully functional ecosystems, and enhance the service functions of various ecosystems.

Article 678 The state shall strengthen the protection of natural resources, adhere to economical and intensive use, coordinate resource protection with development and utilization, formulate plans for the protection and utilization of natural resources, and improve the level of protection and rational utilization of natural resources.

Article 679 The state shall implement compensated use for all types of natural resources according to law, and improve the system of compensated use of natural resources that reflects market supply and demand and the degree of resource scarcity, embodies ecological values, and ensures intergenerational compensation.

Article 680 The state shall establish and improve a system of protected natural areas with national parks as the main body, implement unified establishment, hierarchical management, and zoning control, strengthen systematic protection of important ecosystems, natural relics, natural landscapes, and biodiversity, and meet the people's needs for a beautiful ecological environment, high-quality ecological products, and high-grade ecological services.
The state shall gradually incorporate specific land and sea areas with the most important ecosystems, the most unique natural landscapes, the most essential natural heritage, and the richest biodiversity into national park management, and implement strict protection.
Outside national parks, areas where typical ecosystems, natural concentrated distribution areas of rare and endangered wildlife species, natural relics of special significance, and other protected objects are located shall, according to law, be delineated for a certain area and designated as nature reserves for special protection.
Outside national parks and nature reserves, areas where ecosystems, natural relics, and natural landscapes with ecological, ornamental, cultural, and scientific value are located shall, according to law, be delineated for a certain area and designated as natural parks for long-term protection and sustainable use.

Article 681 The State shall make overall plans and coordinate efforts to promote the protection and restoration of the ecological environment in important river basins such as the Yangtze River and the Yellow River, as well as in key sea areas, with a view to establishing an integrated ecological environment governance system that connects the upstream and downstream of important river basins.
The State shall strengthen ecological protection in important regions such as the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, enhance scientific research on plateau biological species and ecosystems based on the characteristics of the plateau, and increase the capacity to supply ecological products and the service functions of ecosystems.

Article 682 The State shall provide effective protection for important ecosystems, biological species, and biological genetic resources, protect traditional knowledge related to biological diversity, and safeguard biodiversity.

Article 683 The State shall improve the system for the protection and utilization of germplasm resources, and systematically conduct survey, collection, collation, identification, registration, preservation, exchange, and utilization of germplasm resources.

Article 684 Where biological genetic resources of China are provided abroad, or are researched and utilized through cooperation with overseas institutions, individuals, or institutions established or actually controlled by them, approval shall be obtained according to law, and a fair and reasonable national benefit-sharing plan shall be submitted.

Article 685 The State shall strengthen biosafety management, prevent the intrusion of alien species, improve systems for risk monitoring and early warning, investigation and assessment, information release, and emergency response, carry out quarantine supervision of imported animals, plants, and their products according to law, and enhance dynamic tracking and risk assessment of alien species that may be introduced into China.

Article 686 The relevant departments of people's governments at or above the county level may, within their respective functions and duties and based on actual needs, formulate plans in the fields of ecological protection, such as those for forests, grasslands, wetlands, oceans, islands, rivers and lakes, deserts, land, minerals, water, fisheries, protection of wildlife and their habitats, as well as soil and water conservation and desertification prevention and control.

Article 687 The relevant departments of the State Council, including those for ecology and environment, natural resources, water administration, agriculture and rural affairs, forestry and grassland, and standardization, shall, within their respective functions and duties, establish and improve standards concerning the assessment of ecosystem quality and grades, the classification, grading, and economical and intensive use of natural resources, biodiversity conservation, as well as soil and water conservation and ecological restoration.

Article 688 The State shall strengthen the survey and evaluation of the status of natural resources, including land, minerals, forests, grasslands, wetlands, oceans, islands, rivers and lakes, snow mountains and glaciers, deserts, wildlife, and soil and water conservation, and the ecological status, to provide a basis for ensuring ecological security and for the rational development and efficient utilization of territorial space and various natural resources.
The State shall establish and improve a monitoring network system for ecosystems, natural resources, biodiversity, hydrology, meteorology, soil and water conservation, and natural disasters, optimize the layout of monitoring points in important areas, and enhance the capacity for automatic monitoring and early warning.
Survey, evaluation, and monitoring information shall be shared and released in accordance with State regulations to improve the comprehensive management level of ecological protection.

Article 689 The State shall implement a system for the conservation, restoration, and rotation/fallow of cultivated land, and for the rehabilitation of forests, grasslands, wetlands, oceans, and rivers and lakes.
People's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall, according to law, delimit the time and areas for restricted fishing and fishing moratoriums in rivers, lakes, and oceans, restrict the felling of public welfare forests, delimit areas for the prohibition of grazing, rest-grazing, and rotational grazing on grasslands, implement enclosure and protection of desertified land, and may, based on the over-exploitation of groundwater, delimit areas where the extraction of groundwater is prohibited or restricted.

Article 690 The State shall establish a strict system for the prevention, protection, and supervision of soil erosion, and strengthen comprehensive control of desertification, rocky desertification, and soil erosion.
Local people's governments at all levels shall take effective measures to protect and rationally utilize water and soil resources, carry out soil and water conservation, mitigate flood, drought, and wind-sand disasters, prevent land desertification, control desertified land, and protect and improve the ecological environment within their respective administrative areas.

Article 691 In accordance with the integrity, systematic nature, and intrinsic laws of ecosystems, the State shall establish and improve a working mechanism integrating source protection with restoration and governance throughout the entire process; carry out ecological restoration scientifically in accordance with the principle of respecting natural laws, that is, where suitable for forests, plant forests; where suitable for grasslands, plant grasslands; where suitable for deserts, maintain deserts; and where suitable for wastelands, leave wastelands; improve diversified investment mechanisms, encourage and support the participation of social capital, and strengthen the monitoring, supervision, and effectiveness evaluation of ecological restoration, so as to consolidate the achievements of ecological governance.

Article 692 The State shall coordinate urban and rural greening, carry out large-scale land greening actions scientifically, and green and beautify urban and rural areas. Urban and rural greening shall be adapted to local conditions, with scientific selection of greening tree and grass species, strengthen monitoring and evaluation, and meet the needs of health, safety, and livability.

Article 693 The State shall establish a mechanism for the investigation and monitoring of ecological products, and explore the determination of the ownership of rights, responsibilities, and benefits of ecological products through unified confirmation and registration of natural resources.
The State shall establish a mechanism for evaluating the value of ecological products, improve the value accounting methods, and promote the effective transformation of the value of ecological products.
The State shall improve the path for realizing the value of ecological products, which is led by the government, participated by enterprises and all sectors of society, market-oriented, and sustainable, and shall improve the mechanism for the development and operation of ecological products, and expand the channels for realizing the value of ecological products based on local conditions, under the premise of strict protection of the ecological environment.

Article 694 The State shall establish and improve an ecological risk prevention and control system, and take effective measures to improve the capacity and level of ecological risk prevention and control.
People's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall, within their respective functions and duties, carry out ecological disaster prevention, risk assessment, and investigation and treatment of hidden dangers, and take necessary measures for disaster prevention, handling, and post-disaster restoration, so as to prevent and mitigate the impact of disasters.
Where a sudden incident causes or may cause ecological damage, the relevant entity or individual shall immediately take effective measures to eliminate or mitigate the harm, promptly report and notify in accordance with law, and accept investigation and handling.

Article 695 The State shall implement a natural resources inspection and supervision system. The State natural resources inspection and supervision authority shall, according to its authorization, supervise the protection, development, and utilization of natural resources, the implementation of territorial space plans, and the enforcement of relevant laws and regulations by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, as well as by the people's governments of cities determined by the State Council.

Article 696 The State shall adhere to the principle of equality and mutual benefit and win-win cooperation, and support international exchanges and cooperation in fields such as biodiversity, wildlife, marine ecological protection, deep-sea and polar expeditions, desertification prevention and control, and scientific and technological research on ecological protection.
The State shall regulate relevant activities in Antarctica according to law and protect the ecological environment of Antarctica.

Article 697 The State shall adhere to the principles of ecological priority, protection priority, restoration and conservation combined, and sustainable development, strengthen the protection of forest ecosystems and the mountain ranges that serve as important carriers of forests, and give full play to the multiple functions of forests, such as water storage and soil conservation, climate regulation, improvement of the ecological environment, maintenance of biodiversity, and provision of forest products.

Article 698 The competent department of forestry and grassland under the State Council shall be in charge of forestry work nationwide.
The competent departments of forestry and grassland of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be in charge of forestry work within their respective administrative areas.
Township people's governments may designate relevant institutions or assign full-time or part-time personnel to undertake forestry-related work.

Article 699 People's governments at or above the county level shall implement the requirements for territorial space development and protection, rationally plan the structure and layout of forest ecosystem protection and utilization, increase the forest coverage rate and forest stock volume, and improve the quality and stability of forest ecosystems.
The competent departments of forestry and grassland of people's governments at or above the county level may, based on actual needs, organize the formulation of special plans for the protection, restoration, and utilization of forest ecosystems.

Article 700 Afforestation and forest protection are the obligations of citizens.
The State shall organize and encourage afforestation. People's governments at all levels shall organize and carry out nationwide voluntary tree-planting activities, and organize all walks of life and urban and rural residents to carry out afforestation and greening.

Article 701 The State shall strengthen survey and monitoring of forest ecosystems, conducting survey, monitoring, and evaluation of the scale, quality, structure, function, and ecological status of forest ecosystems.

Article 702 The State shall implement a comprehensive protection system for natural forests, strictly restrict the felling of natural forests, strengthen the construction of natural forest management and protection capacity, scientifically implement restoration measures, protect and restore natural forests, and gradually improve the ecological functions of natural forests.

Article 703 The State shall implement classified management of public welfare forests and commercial forests, highlight dominant functions, give play to multiple functions, and cultivate stable, healthy, high-quality, and efficient forest ecosystems.

Article 704 The State shall, based on the needs of ecological protection, designate as public welfare forests those forestlands and forests on forestlands that are ecologically important or ecologically fragile and whose main purpose is to exert ecological benefits.
The State shall implement strict protection of public welfare forests. The competent forestry and grassland departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall, in a planned manner, organize operators of public welfare forests to adopt measures such as stand improvement and forest tending for low-quality and low-efficiency forests in public welfare forests, such as open forests and secondary forests with poor ecological functions, so as to improve the quality and ecological functions of public welfare forests.
Felling in public welfare forests may only be conducted for the purposes of tending, regeneration, and improvement of low-quality and low-efficiency forests, unless otherwise provided by laws and administrative regulations.
Article 705 The State shall protect ancient and famous trees, and prohibits the destruction of ancient and famous trees and their living ecological environment.

Article 706 The State shall, in accordance with law, establish nature reserves in typical forest ecological areas of different natural zones, forest areas where rare animals and plants grow and breed, natural tropical rainforest areas, and other natural forest areas of special protection value, and strengthen protection and management.
The people's governments at or above the county level shall take measures to strengthen the protection of forest wildlife and plants.

Article 707 Local people's governments at all levels shall be responsible for forest fire prevention and extinguishing work within their respective administrative regions, giving play to the role of mass prevention; the people's governments at or above the county level shall organize and lead the emergency management, forestry and grassland, public security, and other relevant departments to work closely together in the scientific prevention, fighting, and handling of forest fires. The national comprehensive fire rescue teams shall undertake the tasks of fighting forest fires and related prevention work as prescribed by the State.

Article 708 The competent forestry and grassland departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the monitoring, quarantine, and prevention and control of forest pests within their respective administrative regions.
The competent forestry and grassland departments of the people's governments at or above the provincial level shall be responsible for determining the quarantine pests of forest plants and their products, and delineating epidemic areas and protected areas.
The prevention and control of major forest pest disasters shall be under the responsibility of local people's governments. When outbreaks of explosive, hazardous, or other major forest pest disasters occur, the local people's government shall promptly organize their elimination.
Forest operators, under the support and guidance of the government, shall carry out prevention and control of forest pests within their management and operation scope.

Article 709 It is prohibited to engage in activities such as clearing forests for cultivation, quarrying, sand mining, soil extraction, and other acts that destroy trees and forestlands.
It is prohibited to cut firewood, destroy seedlings, or graze livestock in young forestlands.
It is prohibited to move or damage forest protection signs without authorization.

Article 710 Local people's governments shall organize relevant departments to establish forest protection organizations responsible for forest protection work; build forest protection facilities according to actual needs, and strengthen the protection of forest ecosystems; urge relevant organizations to conclude forest protection covenants, organize the masses to protect forests, designate forest protection responsibility areas, and assign full-time or part-time forest rangers.

Article 711 The State shall enhance the functions of forest ecosystems, increase the supply capacity of ecological products, provide excellent air and beautiful ecological environment for human life and production, and give play to ecological values such as leisure and recreation, scientific research, and education.
The development and utilization of forest resources shall not destroy the living environment of forest wildlife and plants, and shall not damage the functions of forest ecosystems.

Article 712 The protection of grassland ecosystems shall adhere to scientific planning, comprehensive protection, focused restoration, and rational utilization, giving play to multiple functions of grasslands, such as regulating climate, conserving water sources, retaining soil and water, preventing wind and fixing sand, and serving as living environments for wildlife and plants, so as to promote the virtuous cycle of grassland ecosystems and the sustainable utilization of resources.

Article 713 The competent forestry and grassland department under the State Council shall be in charge of the supervision and management of grasslands nationwide.
The competent forestry and grassland departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall be in charge of the supervision and management of grasslands within their respective administrative regions.
The people's governments of townships and towns shall strengthen the supervision and inspection of the protection, restoration, and utilization of grasslands within their administrative regions, and may, as needed, appoint full-time or part-time personnel responsible for specific supervision and inspection work.

Article 714 The competent forestry and grassland departments of the people's governments at or above the county level may, based on actual needs, work together with relevant departments to organize the formulation of special plans for grassland protection, restoration, utilization, and the like.

Article 715 The State shall strengthen the investigation of grassland ecosystems. The competent forestry and grassland departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall, together with relevant departments, conduct investigations on the area, grade, grass yield, carrying capacity, and ecosystem stability of grasslands.
The State shall establish grassland production and ecological monitoring and early warning systems. The competent forestry and grassland departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall, together with relevant departments, carry out dynamic monitoring of basic grassland conditions, including area, grade, vegetation composition, productivity, ecological health status, natural disasters, and biological disasters, and promptly provide dynamic monitoring and early warning information services to the people's government at the same level and relevant departments.

Article 716 The State shall implement a basic grassland protection system, designating as basic grasslands, in accordance with law, those grasslands that play the most fundamental and important role in maintaining ecological security and ensuring the healthy development of grassland animal husbandry, and shall implement strict protection and management to ensure that the area does not decrease, the quality does not decline, and the use does not change.

Article 717 The State shall strengthen the protection of grassland wildlife and plants, establish grassland-type nature reserves in accordance with law, enhance the integrity and connectivity of grassland ecosystems, strengthen the protection of wildlife habitats, migration corridors, and growing environments of wild plants, ensure the space for wildlife and plants to survive and reproduce, and protect the biodiversity of grasslands.

Article 718 Local people's governments at all levels shall be responsible for grassland fire prevention and extinguishing work within their respective administrative regions, giving play to the role of mass prevention; the people's governments at or above the county level shall organize the emergency management, forestry and grassland, public security, and other relevant departments to work closely together in the scientific prevention, fighting, and handling of grassland fires. The national comprehensive fire rescue teams shall undertake the tasks of fighting grassland fires and related prevention work as prescribed by the State.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall properly organize and manage the scientific prevention and control of rodent pests, diseases, and poisonous weeds in grasslands.

Article 719 The development and utilization of grasslands shall not destroy the living environment of grassland wildlife and plants, and shall not damage the functions of grassland ecosystems.
The State shall implement a system of determining livestock numbers based on grass yield and balancing grass and livestock to prevent overloading and overgrazing. The competent forestry and grassland departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the grassland carrying capacity standards formulated by the competent forestry and grassland department under the State Council, and taking into account local actual conditions and the reasonable needs for wildlife survival and reproduction, periodically verify the grassland carrying capacity.
The State shall implement grazing bans and rest grazing for grasslands that are severely degraded, desertified, salinized, or rocky, as well as grasslands in ecologically fragile areas, and shall provide subsidies or rewards to farmers and herders who implement grazing bans, rest grazing, and grass-livestock balance.

Article 720 It is prohibited to reclaim grasslands. For reclaimed grasslands that suffer from serious soil erosion, show a trend of desertification, or need to improve the ecological environment, the conversion of farmland back to grasslands shall be carried out in a planned and step-by-step manner; where desertification, salinization, or rocky desertification has already been caused, the situation shall be remedied within a prescribed time limit.
It is prohibited to dig up plants or engage in other activities that destroy grassland vegetation in deserts, semi-deserts, and grasslands that are severely degraded, desertified, salinized, rocky, or suffering from soil erosion, as well as grasslands in ecologically fragile areas, unless otherwise provided by laws and administrative regulations.

Article 721 The State shall protect, restore, and rationally utilize grasslands. On the basis of protecting grassland ecology, the State shall guide the scientific development of grassland eco-tourism, ecological education, scientific research and other activities, so as to bring into play the ecological value of grasslands.

Article 722 The State shall adhere to the principles of protection priority, strict management, systematic governance, scientific restoration, and rational utilization, improve the protection system for wetland ecosystems, give full play to the multiple ecological functions of wetlands such as water conservation, climate regulation, improvement of the ecological environment, and maintenance of biodiversity, and achieve the unification of ecological, social and economic benefits.

Article 723 The competent department of forestry and grassland under the State Council shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of wetland resources, the formulation of wetland protection plans and relevant national standards, the supervision and administration of wetland development and utilization, and the ecological protection and restoration of wetlands. Other relevant departments under the State Council, such as those of natural resources, water administration, housing and urban-rural construction, ecological environment, and agriculture and rural affairs, shall, within their respective functions and duties, undertake work related to wetland protection, restoration, and management.
The competent department of forestry and grassland under the State Council shall, together with the competent departments of natural resources, water administration, housing and urban-rural construction, ecological environment, and agriculture and rural affairs under the State Council, establish a coordination and information notification mechanism for wetland protection.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the coordination of wetland protection, be responsible for wetland protection within their respective administrative regions, and take measures to maintain the stability of wetland areas and enhance wetland ecological functions. The relevant departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions and duties, be responsible for work related to wetland protection, restoration, and management.

Article 724 The competent department of forestry and grassland under the State Council shall, together with relevant departments, formulate a national wetland protection plan according to law.
The competent departments of forestry and grassland of local people's governments at or above the county level may, as needed, together with relevant departments, formulate wetland protection plans for their respective administrative regions.

Article 725 The competent department of natural resources under the State Council shall, together with the competent department of forestry and grassland and other relevant departments under the State Council, conduct surveys on the types, distribution, area, biodiversity, protection and utilization of wetlands nationwide, and establish a unified information release and sharing mechanism.
The competent department of forestry and grassland under the State Council shall carry out dynamic monitoring of nationally important wetlands in accordance with monitoring technical specifications, and shall, based on the monitoring data, assess the ecological status of nationally important wetlands and release early warning information in accordance with the provisions.

Article 726 The State shall classify wetlands into important wetlands and general wetlands based on their ecological location, area, and the importance of maintaining ecological functions and biodiversity, and implement graded management.
Article 727 The State shall implement a total wetland area control system, and incorporate the targets for total wetland area control into the wetland protection target responsibility system.

Article 728 The State shall strictly control the occupation of wetlands. Where occupation is truly necessary, the relevant procedures shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the Wetland Protection Law of the People's Republic of China.
Where temporary use of wetlands is necessary, the relevant procedures shall be handled according to law, and no permanent buildings may be constructed. After the expiration of the period of temporary use of wetlands, the land-using unit or individual shall restore the wetland area and ecological conditions.
Except for the occupation of wetlands within the management scope of river courses and flood storage and detention areas due to flood control, navigation, ports, or other water projects, the unit that has been approved according to law to occupy important wetlands shall, based on local natural conditions, restore or reconstruct wetlands equivalent to the area and quality of the occupied wetlands; if restoration or reconstruction is not possible, the unit shall pay a wetland restoration fee.

Article 729 Local people's governments and their relevant departments shall take measures to prevent and control the adverse impacts of human activities on wetlands and their biodiversity, strengthen wetland pollution prevention and control, mitigate wetland degradation caused by human and natural factors, and maintain the stability of wetland ecological functions.
